title: Sensitivity analyses vary one violated assumption at a time when several are violated together
text: UCF-02 Unverifiable High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: Sensitivity analyses vary one violated assumption at a time when several are violated together
text:
Statement
A conventional emulation reports a point estimate under exchangeability, positivity and correct measurement, then a sensitivity analysis relaxing one of them. In a longitudinal emulation on routine data several are doubtful at once, and one-at-a-time analyses need not characterize their joint effect. Joint multi-bias analysis of confounding, selection and misclassification exists, with software, and so do longitudinal sensitivity models for sequential confounding. What is not standard, and not required by any reporting practice, is a joint region that also includes practical positivity failure under sustained-strategy g-methods, with the product of marginal analyses remaining the default in practice. Constructing one requires compatible bias parameters, restrictions on how the biases depend on each other, and a stated target population and estimand; without those restrictions the resulting bounds can be vacuous, and the partial-identification set has to be reported as distinct from finite-sample uncertainty.

title: Sensitivity analyses vary one violated assumption at a time when several are violated together
text:
Why it is open
Bias parameters for different violations live on different scales and enter the estimating equations at different points, so there is no natural single-parameter family to sweep, and the dependence restrictions that make the region informative are themselves assumptions nobody can check. The joint region is typically not a product of the marginal regions, so the computationally convenient answer is also the wrong one, and the correct one can be uninformative. Reporting a wide identification region is professionally costly, since it makes an honest analysis look weaker than a naive one and no journal requires it.

title: Sensitivity analyses vary one violated assumption at a time when several are violated together
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Extend the existing joint multi-bias machinery to include practical positivity failure under sustained-strategy g-methods, which is the violation current joint analyses omit. Specify compatible bias parameters and explicit dependence restrictions, state the target population and estimand, and report the partial-identification set separately from the sampling interval so a reader can see which part more data would reduce. Establish by simulation how far the product of marginal sensitivity analyses misstates the joint region, since that approximation is the current default.

title: Sensitivity analyses vary one violated assumption at a time when several are violated together
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source said. “A conventional emulation reports a point estimate under exchangeability, positivity and correct measurement, and then a sensitivity analysis that relaxes one of them. In a longitudinal emulation on routine data all of them are doubtful simultaneously: unmeasured confounding, selection into the cohort, misclassification of exposure and outcome, and practical positivity failure all operate at once and interact. There is little theory for the joint case, so the reported uncertainty is a sampling interval around a point that is identified only under a conjunction the analysis has already conceded is false. What is missing is a way to report an identification region reflecting all the violations together, separately from the sampling interval.”
What was wrong with it. Theory and software for joint multi-bias analysis of confounding, selection and misclassification do exist, and some longitudinal sequential-confounding sensitivity models with them, so the claim that there is little theory for the joint case was too broad. Two things also have to be said about the joint region: it needs compatible bias parameters, dependence restrictions, a stated target population and estimand, and without those restrictions the resulting bounds can be vacuous.
Dissent. grok dissented (overstated): The agenda claim that there is little theory for joint violations is not faithful. Multi-bias quantitative bias analysis is textbook material (Lash–Fox–Fink), with simultaneous adjustment methods, multiple-bias bounds, and released software. Smith, Mathur, and VanderWeele (2021) give composite bounds for unmeasured confounding, selection, and differential exposure/outcome misclassification and explicitly warn that one-at-a-time analysis can misstate joint impact. Brendel, Torres, and Arah (2023) develop simultaneous multi-bias adjustment via imputation and/or regression weighting for uncontrolled confounding, selection bias, and misclassification together; the CRAN package multibias (v1.7.3, still maintained 2026) implements that framework and advertises use for observational longitudinal real-world evidence. The EValue ecosystem documents multiple-bias bound examples. Gerlach-Wood et al. (2025) review QBA software and catalog tools that adjust several bias sources simultaneously (multibias, episensr variants, others), while still noting gaps and uneven simultaneous versus sequential implementations. For longitudinal time-varying treatment settings closer to sustained-strategy emulation, Tan (2025, Biometrika) formulates multi-period sensitivity models under sequential unmeasured confounding and contrasts joint versus product sensitivity models, which directly engages the report’s point that product-of-marginals can be the wrong answer. These works partially deliver the proposed direction: modular bias parameters, joint regions or adjusted estimates under several systematic errors, and (in probabilistic QBA) separation of systematic from sampling uncertainty. They do not fully close the problem as stated for a complete longitudinal g-methods target trial emulation in which unmeasured confounding, selection, measurement error, and practical positivity failure all enter one modular identification region reported as standard practice. Gao et al. (2025, Biometrics) still describe joint multi-assumption sensitivity for externally controlled trials as largely unexplored outside their omnibus contribution, which is useful counterweight to over-claiming full solution. No journal mandate for joint identification regions in TTE was found; professional cost of wide regions remains a social, not a mathematical, barrier. Package checks of TrialEmulation/gfoRmula/lmtp did not show native multi-bias identification-region reporting. So the correct status is partial solution of the joint multi-bias theory/software agenda for standard observational designs, with residual open work for full sustained-strategy TTE g-method modules and for ID-region-versus-sampling-interval reporting as a field norm. The claim of little joint theory is overstated relative to Smith–VanderWeele bounds, Brendel simultaneous multi-bias, multibias software, and Tan’s joint longitudinal sensitivity models.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. No work in the corpus reports a joint identification region over simultaneous unmeasured confounding, selection, misclassification and positivity failure in a longitudinal emulation, nor separates an identification region from a sampling interval in its reporting. Multiverse analysis of design choices is the nearest neighbor and varies design rather than bias parameters. The absence is consistent with the entry, and the confidence is capped because a partial-identification literature exists outside the eight search phrases used to build this corpus and would not have been retrieved.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Joint sensitivity analysis is a valid open workflow problem, but the statement treats possible threats as known simultaneous violations. Cohort selection is not necessarily bias for an estimand defined in that cohort, exposure or outcome misclassification need not be material, and practical near-positivity is an estimation problem rather than the structural nonpositivity that destroys identification. Performing a sensitivity analysis also does not concede that the identifying assumption is false. Interaction means one-at-a-time analyses generally cannot be combined mechanically; it does not imply that a Cartesian joint parameter space is always wrong. Without restrictions, simultaneous arbitrary confounding, selection, misclassification, and structural nonpositivity generally produce vacuous causal-effect bounds. A nontrivial identification region therefore requires explicit bounds and a coherent joint bias model. Bayesian sampling with priors on unidentified bias parameters yields a prior-sensitive posterior, not an identification region. More data can sometimes inform validation parameters or alleviate practical overlap problems, and omitted bias can point toward or away from a claim, so the asserted systematic understatement that always favors the claim is false. No R or Python package capability is asserted here.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / overstated. The agenda claim that there is little theory for joint violations is not faithful. Multi-bias quantitative bias analysis is textbook material (Lash–Fox–Fink), with simultaneous adjustment methods, multiple-bias bounds, and released software. Smith, Mathur, and VanderWeele (2021) give composite bounds for unmeasured confounding, selection, and differential exposure/outcome misclassification and explicitly warn that one-at-a-time analysis can misstate joint impact. Brendel, Torres, and Arah (2023) develop simultaneous multi-bias adjustment via imputation and/or regression weighting for uncontrolled confounding, selection bias, and misclassification together; the CRAN package multibias (v1.7.3, still maintained 2026) implements that framework and advertises use for observational longitudinal real-world evidence. The EValue ecosystem documents multiple-bias bound examples. Gerlach-Wood et al. (2025) review QBA software and catalog tools that adjust several bias sources simultaneously (multibias, episensr variants, others), while still noting gaps and uneven simultaneous versus sequential implementations. For longitudinal time-varying treatment settings closer to sustained-strategy emulation, Tan (2025, Biometrika) formulates multi-period sensitivity models under sequential unmeasured confounding and contrasts joint versus product sensitivity models, which directly engages the report’s point that product-of-marginals can be the wrong answer. These works partially deliver the proposed direction: modular bias parameters, joint regions or adjusted estimates under several systematic errors, and (in probabilistic QBA) separation of systematic from sampling uncertainty. They do not fully close the problem as stated for a complete longitudinal g-methods target trial emulation in which unmeasured confounding, selection, measurement error, and practical positivity failure all enter one modular identification region reported as standard practice. Gao et al. (2025, Biometrics) still describe joint multi-assumption sensitivity for externally controlled trials as largely unexplored outside their omnibus contribution, which is useful counterweight to over-claiming full solution. No journal mandate for joint identification regions in TTE was found; professional cost of wide regions remains a social, not a mathematical, barrier. Package checks of TrialEmulation/gfoRmula/lmtp did not show native multi-bias identification-region reporting. So the correct status is partial solution of the joint multi-bias theory/software agenda for standard observational designs, with residual open work for full sustained-strategy TTE g-method modules and for ID-region-versus-sampling-interval reporting as a field norm. The claim of little joint theory is overstated relative to Smith–VanderWeele bounds, Brendel simultaneous multi-bias, multibias software, and Tan’s joint longitudinal sensitivity models. Cites 10.1097/EDE.0000000000001380: Gives a composite bound and sensitivity analysis for the joint impact of unmeasured confounding, selection bias, and differential exposure or outcome misclassification on a risk ratio, with explicit warning that one-at-a-time analysis can under- or over-state joint bias; implements the multiple-bias bound in the EValue tooling.. Cites 10.1093/ije/dyad001: Proposes simultaneous (not merely sequential) multi-bias adjustment for uncontrolled confounding, selection bias, and misclassification via imputation and/or regression weighting, evaluated as a joint alternative to one-bias-at-a-time analysis.. Cites 10.32614/CRAN.package.multibias: Released, maintained R software that simultaneously adjusts for any combination of uncontrolled confounding, exposure/outcome misclassification, and selection bias, based on Brendel et al. (2023), and marketed for observational longitudinal real-world evidence.. Cites 10.1093/biomet/asae044: Develops multi-period sensitivity models and sharp/conservative bounds for longitudinal causal effects under sequential unmeasured confounding, and formulates joint versus product sensitivity models, addressing interaction of time-indexed assumption violations rather than a single one-at-a-time parameter..

glm

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and correctly scoped as a gap in current practice and available theory rather than a structural impossibility. The reasons given for it being open (bias parameters living on different scales, non-product joint regions due to interactions, and professional costs) genuinely support the claim that joint sensitivity analyses are not standard and lack established, convenient theory. The severity is proportionate to the methodological gap.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1/4) → R7:counter-and-support-both-present(support=2/counter=1)

title: No outcome-blind procedure selects the time grid or the grace period
text: TZO-01 Confirmed open Very high priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: No outcome-blind procedure selects the time grid or the grace period
text:
Statement
An emulated protocol has to fix three times that a randomized trial fixes in one act, when eligibility is assessed, when treatment is assigned, and when follow-up begins, and it has to fix the resolution at which time is measured, because routine data arrive as dated records rather than as scheduled visits. Clone-censor-weight and sequential emulation handle the misalignment; neither chooses the grace period or the interval width, and estimates move with both. A coarse interval lets treatment affect an outcome inside the interval before censoring applies; a fine interval produces high-dimensional nuisance models and unstable weights. Selection tools exist and use outcome information: cross-validated variance has been evaluated as a measure of data support for choosing a discretization. What does not exist is a procedure that selects either quantity from the treatment and observation processes alone with outcome labels masked, and treatment and observation processes without further clinical and causal assumptions cannot identify a uniquely meaningful grace period or guarantee that a grid preserves the relevant ordering. Alternative grace periods are different treatment strategies rather than alternative specifications of one, and are presented as sensitivity analyses of a single estimand.

title: No outcome-blind procedure selects the time grid or the grace period
text:
Why it is open
The choice is made before any model is fitted, so no model can price it, and selecting by fit to the outcome is the one move that would make it a statistical problem and the move that induces selection. The clinically meaningful interval is a property of the disease and the care process rather than of the data, and no purely data-driven criterion recovers it. Published emulations overwhelmingly report a single specification: a systematic review of 14 comparative studies found the grace period unreported in 36% and ranging from 0 to 180 days when reported, with no study conducting a sensitivity analysis on it.

title: No outcome-blind procedure selects the time grid or the grace period
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Hernán MA, Sauer BC, Hernández-Díaz S, Platt R, Shrier I. Specifying a target trial prevents immortal time bias and other self-inflicted injuries in observational analyses. J Clin Epidemiol 2016
Names the misalignment of eligibility, assignment and follow-up as the source of immortal time bias and shows that specifying the trial removes it. Treats the grace period as given.


Cain LE, Robins JM, Lanoy E, Logan R, Costagliola D, Hernán MA. Using observational data to emulate a randomized trial of dynamic treatment-switching strategies. Int J Epidemiol 2016;45(6):2038-2049
Works an emulation with grace periods and dynamic switching, establishing the design without a criterion for the grace period’s length.


Maringe C, Benitez Majano S, Exarchakou A, et al. Reflection on modern methods: trial emulation in the presence of immortal-time bias. Int J Epidemiol 2020;49(5):1719-1729
A worked clone-censor-weight example that makes the artificial censoring and its weights explicit.


Ferreira Guerra S, et al. Impact of discretization of the timeline for longitudinal causal inference methods. Stat Med 2020
Shows that discretization changes the parameter and loses confounder information, and evaluates cross-validated variance as a data-support criterion for choosing a discretization. A selection tool, and not an outcome-blind one.


Optimal CD4 count for initiating HIV treatment: impact of CD4 observation frequency and grace periods, and performance of dynamic marginal structural models. Epidemiology 2014
Quantifies how the optimal dynamic regime shifts with observation frequency and grace-period length.


Impact of time zero designation on estimated COVID-19 antiviral effectiveness in observational studies. Am J Epidemiol 2026
Compares five time-zero designations in one cohort, a worked example of the multiverse this entry asks for.


Reporting and variability of constructing medication treatment episodes in pharmacoepidemiology studies: a meta-epidemiological review. Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf 2020
Finds the grace period unreported in 36% of 14 studies and ranging from 0 to 180 days when reported, with no study conducting a sensitivity analysis on the assumption.


Tankpinou Zoumenou H, et al. Time Partitioning in Target Trial Emulation. arXiv 2026
Treats time partitioning as an unresolved problem in its own right rather than an implementation detail.

title: No outcome-blind procedure selects the time grid or the grace period
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Prespecify an outcome-blind grid rule and report post-lock comparisons across plausible grids that hold the estimand fixed, so what varies is the discretization rather than the question. Present alternative grace periods as different treatment strategies with their own estimands, not as a sensitivity analysis of one. Compare landmarking, sequential trials, continuous-time g-computation, counting-process marginal structural models and clone-censor-weighting on the same generated data, scoring the proportion of within-interval ordering conflicts alongside bias and coverage, and report grid invariance as a diagnostic while stating that it reveals sensitivity rather than establishing identification.

title: No outcome-blind procedure selects the time grid or the grace period
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “An emulated protocol has to fix three times that a randomized trial fixes in one act: when eligibility is assessed, when treatment is assigned, and when follow-up begins. It also has to fix the resolution at which time is measured, because routine data arrive as dated records rather than as a schedule of study visits. Clone-censor-weight and sequential emulation both handle the misalignment itself, but neither chooses the grace period or the interval width, and estimates move with both. A coarse interval lets treatment affect an outcome inside the interval before censoring is applied; a fine interval produces high-dimensional nuisance models and unstable weights. What does not exist is a procedure that selects either quantity from the treatment and observation processes alone, without touching outcome information, together with a reported measure of how far the estimate would have moved under the alternatives.”
What was wrong with it. Two additions. A selection tool for the time grid does exist, using cross-validated variance as a measure of data support, and it uses outcome information, so it is a procedure and not an outcome-blind one. And alternative grace periods are not competing specifications of one estimand: they define different treatment strategies and potentially different estimands, so presenting them as a sensitivity analysis misdescribes what is varying.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The claim has more prior work behind it than the entry admits, and the work does not close it. Ferreira Guerra et al. investigate exactly the selection question for the time grid, showing that different discretizations change both the parameter and the information retained about time-dependent confounders, and evaluating cross-validated variance as a criterion for choosing one. That is a selection procedure, so the entry’s flat claim that none exists is wrong. It is not an outcome-blind procedure, which is what the entry’s own title asks for, so the qualified claim survives. On the empirical side the entry is understated rather than overstated: a systematic review of 14 DPP-4 inhibitor studies found grace periods unreported in 36% and ranging from 0 to 180 days when reported, with no study conducting a sensitivity analysis on the assumption. A 2026 study designating time zero five different ways in the same nirmatrelvir-ritonavir cohort supplies the sensitivity evidence the entry says the field lacks. Sperling and colleagues showed in 2014 that the optimal dynamic regime itself moves with CD4 observation frequency and grace-period length, which is a stronger version of the entry’s claim and predates it by a decade. Supporting quotation retained here rather than as counter-evidence: [10.1002/pds.5071] Grace period was not reported in 5 (35.7%) studies and ranged from 0 days to 180 days when reported … No studies conducted sensitivity analyses examining the effects of these assumptions on study findings. Cites 10.1002/sim.8710: Shows that discretization changes the parameter and loses confounder information, and evaluates cross-validated variance as a data-support criterion for choosing a discretization with pooled longitudinal TMLE. This is a selection tool, so the entry must not claim none exists; it uses outcome information, so the outcome-blind claim stands.. Cites 10.1097/ede.0000000000000043: Quantifies how the optimal dynamic regime shifts with observation frequency and grace-period length, establishing the dependence the entry describes.. Cites 10.1093/aje/kwaf221: Compares five time-zero designations in one cohort, which is the multiverse over time zero that the entry proposes as a direction and which therefore already has a worked example..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. A narrower methodological gap remains open, but the statement conflates protocol definition, discretization, and sensitivity analysis. The grace period is part of the sustained treatment strategy: changing it generally changes the adherence rule and causal estimand, so movement across grace periods is not sensitivity of one fixed effect. Grid width can instead be a measurement or numerical-approximation choice, and grid stability is interpretable only when nested grids preserve the treatment strategy, event-ordering convention, and underlying continuous-time estimand. Treatment and visit processes alone cannot guarantee a causally adequate grid because data-generating processes with identical treatment and observation laws can have different within-interval outcome timing. Nevertheless, an outcome-blind selection rule can be prespecified and frozen, after which outcomes can be used to report a multiverse without outcome-driven selection. Coarse intervals do not inevitably reverse treatment-outcome ordering when exact timestamps are retained, and fine intervals do not inevitably create high-dimensional nuisance models or unstable weights; those consequences depend on event-time resolution, model parameterization, and positivity. Misaligned time zero and lost temporal ordering can be critical, but the absence of an automatic selector is a roadmap issue rather than uniformly very-high severity. The literature-wide assertion that no procedure exists is not established under the assigned technical-only lens.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Inverted-prior search did not turn up an outcome-blind procedure that selects the time-grid width or grace-period length from treatment and observation processes alone and reports how far the estimate moves under alternatives. The report’s own core citation, Tankpinou Zoumenou et al. (arXiv:2603.15924, 2026), formalizes when partitioning is too fine or too coarse via structural causal models, shows that clone-censor-weight can fail when treatment affects outcome inside a period, and recommends clinical specification of partitioning rather than defaulting to data resolution. That is design guidance and a validity check, not an algorithmic, outcome-masked selector. Wanis et al. (JRSS-A 2024; arXiv:2212.11398) formalizes natural versus stochastic grace-period strategies (how treatment is distributed during a grace window) and leaves window length as a protocol input. Ferreira Guerra et al. (Stat Med 2020) and Adams, Saria, and Rosenblum (arXiv:2011.15099) quantify estimation consequences of timeline discretization; they do not choose the grid without outcome use. Continuous-time MSMs and marked-point-process weights (Ryalen/Røysland line; Kalia et al., Stat Med 2025) reduce dependence on an arbitrary binning for some sustained-treatment estimands, but they do not select a grace period, do not fix the eligibility–assignment–follow-up triad for clone or sequential emulations, and do not ship a grid-invariance diagnostic. TARGET (JAMA 2025), HARPER/STaRT-RWE-style protocol templates, and Fu et al. (BMJ 2026) require reporting interval width and grace period and teach alignment; none supply a data-only selection rule. Applied emulations often vary grace period in one-off sensitivity analyses (for example six versus twelve months); that is ad hoc robustness, not outcome-blind primary selection plus a multiverse movement measure. CRAN/GitHub surfaces for TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, gfoRmulaICE, lmtp, ltmle, concrete, CICI, WeightIt, ipw, adjustedCurves, riskRegression, zEpid, and related tools treat interval unit and grace length as user arguments, with no merged PR implementing outcome-masked grid or grace selection. Queries covered the problem’s prior_work list; grace-period/time-grid/partitioning terms in AJE, Epidemiology, IJE, EJE, JCE, PDS, Stat Med, Biometrics/Biostatistics, BMJ/JAMA family, 2024–2026; arXiv stat.ME and medRxiv; multiverse/specification-curve + grace or time-zero; continuous-time MSM/g-computation; visit-intensity or observation-process interval selection; and package activity. Proposal, formalization, and sensitivity practice leave the stated gap open.

glm

open / supported. The claim asserts a methodological gap: no outcome-blind procedure currently exists for selecting the time grid or grace period, nor is there a standard for reporting sensitivity to these choices. The reason given (that outcome-based selection induces selection bias, and clinical intervals are not purely data-driven) coherently supports why this gap exists and why it remains open. The claim is pitched at the right level of generality, describing a current absence in practice rather than a structural impossibility, as evidenced by the proposed direction to build such a procedure.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: Code, phenotype logic, weight diagnostics and rejected protocol versions are not available for emulations
text: SFW-03 Partially addressed High priority Promising Tractability 5/5

title: Code, phenotype logic, weight diagnostics and rejected protocol versions are not available for emulations
text:
Statement
The TARGET statement asks for the target protocol, its data mapping, the estimands, the assumptions, the estimates and the sensitivity analyses, and is a transparency instrument rather than a risk-of-bias certification. An emulation is not externally auditable when its final analysis code, its complete versioned phenotype logic and its weight diagnostics are unavailable, and in current practice they are: most emulations are irreproducible in operative detail despite faithful protocol reporting. Where the real data cannot be shared, code plus a documented schema, a container and synthetic fixtures establishes that the pipeline executes and what it does; it does not reproduce the published estimate, and auditability rather than reproduction is what such a release can deliver. Material protocol amendments belong in a versioned decision log, which nothing currently requires.

title: Code, phenotype logic, weight diagnostics and rejected protocol versions are not available for emulations
text:
Why it is open
Phenotype logic is often held under license or embedded in institutional tooling, so publishing it is a legal and technical problem rather than a willingness problem. Analysis code depends on a data model the reader cannot obtain, which makes released code unrunnable and therefore feel pointless to release, and the answer, a synthetic fixture, is extra work that benefits nobody in the authoring group. Rejected protocol versions are not artifacts anyone currently keeps, so there is nothing to publish even where there is a will to.

title: Code, phenotype logic, weight diagnostics and rejected protocol versions are not available for emulations
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Hansford HJ, Cashin AG, Jones MD, et al. Transparent reporting of observational studies emulating a target trial: the TARGET statement. JAMA 2025
Establishes the reporting standard for emulations, whose purpose is transparency rather than risk-of-bias certification.


Su L, et al. TrialEmulation: an R package to emulate target trials for causal analysis of observational time-to-event data. arXiv 2024
Provides a reference implementation for sequence expansion and weighting, which is the level at which reproducibility becomes achievable rather than aspirational.

title: Code, phenotype logic, weight diagnostics and rejected protocol versions are not available for emulations
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Publish machine-readable protocols, complete phenotype logic with code-set versions, weight diagnostics, a documented schema, a container and synthetic fixtures that exercise the pipeline end to end, and state that the target is external auditability rather than numerical reproduction. Retain material protocol amendments in a versioned decision log. Pair the reporting checklist with RECORD and STROBE and with a causal risk-of-bias assessment, so reporting, provenance and appraisal are separately satisfied rather than conflated.

title: Code, phenotype logic, weight diagnostics and rejected protocol versions are not available for emulations
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “The TARGET statement asks for the target protocol, its data mapping, the estimands, the assumptions, the estimates and the sensitivity analyses, and it is a transparency instrument rather than a risk-of-bias certification. What remains unavailable in practice is the material that would let someone re-run the study: the analysis code, the complete phenotype logic including the code lists and their versions, the weight diagnostics, and the protocol versions that were tried and rejected. An emulation is a long pipeline in which most of the decisions are expressed in code rather than in prose, so a paper that reports the protocol faithfully can still be irreproducible in every operative detail.”
What was wrong with it. Releasing code with a documented schema, a container and synthetic fixtures establishes executability and does not reproduce the published estimate, so the entry’s implied goal was the wrong one. What such a release achieves is external auditability of the operative decisions, which is worth stating as the target rather than reproduction.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): The corpus contains reporting standards, quality assessment tools and comprehensive analyses of emulation practice, and none requires or reports the release of analysis code, complete phenotype logic with code-set versions, weight diagnostics or simulated test data. The automated-code-generation paper implies the artifacts exist in machine-readable form, which strengthens the entry: the material could be released and is not. grok dissented (supported): Inverted prior: assume executable code, versioned phenotypes, weight diagnostics, and rejected protocols are already standard deliverables. TARGET (Cashin/Hansford et al., JAMA/BMJ 2025) is correctly scoped as a reporting checklist for protocol, mapping, estimands, assumptions, estimates, and sensitivity analyses; it is not a risk-of-bias instrument and does not require analysis code, code-list versions, weight diagnostics dumps, or failed protocol versions. That part of the claim stands.
Partial prior art exists in infrastructure, not in universal publication norms. OHDSI Phenotype Library is a public, version-controlled phenotype repository with release versioning and DOIs for cohort definitions (partial answer to phenotype logic and code-set versions, limited to OMOP/OHDSI contributors). Strategus/HADES encode analyses as shareable JSON-plus-R workflows on OMOP. THESEUS (Kim et al., medRxiv 2026.03.13.26348306) automates mapping free-text TTE descriptions to Strategus JSON and executable R, improving shareable machine-readable specs for OHDSI-style studies; it does not compel release of rejected protocols or non-OMOP phenotype licenses. Scattered tutorials (e.g. Hoffman steroids-trial-emulation with simulated data) and TrialEmulation show that reference code can be released, which does not make re-runnable artifacts common for applied emulations on licensed claims/EHR. Queries run: TARGET reproducibility code phenotype; OHDSI Phenotype Library; THESEUS Strategus TTE; STaRT-RWE HARPER code sharing; RECORD-PE STROBE rejected protocol versions. No 2025–2026 guidance requires publishing rejected protocol versions or institution-exportable simulated test datasets as the standard companion to TARGET. Legal and data-model barriers named in the problem remain. Partial solve for OHDSI-adjacent machine-readable design; field-wide unavailability of code, full phenotypes, weight diagnostics, and rejected versions remains open.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. The corpus contains reporting standards, quality assessment tools and comprehensive analyses of emulation practice, and none requires or reports the release of analysis code, complete phenotype logic with code-set versions, weight diagnostics or simulated test data. The automated-code-generation paper implies the artifacts exist in machine-readable form, which strengthens the entry: the material could be released and is not. Cites 10.1093/jamiaopen/ooag131: Produces the executable specification as an artifact, which shows the material a reproducibility requirement would ask for is producible..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The reproducibility objective is technically sound, but the report turns a variable practice deficit into a universal claim. Code tied to an inaccessible data model is still useful when accompanied by a schema, adapters, containers, or synthetic fixtures. Version control and protocol registries can retain amendments, so it is false that rejected versions are artifacts nobody keeps. Synthetic test data can establish executability and exercise phenotype and weighting logic, but cannot reproduce or validate the real-data estimate. Final analysis code, versioned phenotype definitions, and weight diagnostics are decision-critical; publication of every discarded draft is a lower-priority provenance demand and is better framed as a prospective amendment and decision log. The pinned TrialEmulation source supports the narrower claim that reusable sequence-expansion and weighting machinery exists, but it cannot supply study-specific phenotype logic or release artifacts.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported. Inverted prior: assume executable code, versioned phenotypes, weight diagnostics, and rejected protocols are already standard deliverables. TARGET (Cashin/Hansford et al., JAMA/BMJ 2025) is correctly scoped as a reporting checklist for protocol, mapping, estimands, assumptions, estimates, and sensitivity analyses; it is not a risk-of-bias instrument and does not require analysis code, code-list versions, weight diagnostics dumps, or failed protocol versions. That part of the claim stands.


Partial prior art exists in infrastructure, not in universal publication norms. OHDSI Phenotype Library is a public, version-controlled phenotype repository with release versioning and DOIs for cohort definitions (partial answer to phenotype logic and code-set versions, limited to OMOP/OHDSI contributors). Strategus/HADES encode analyses as shareable JSON-plus-R workflows on OMOP. THESEUS (Kim et al., medRxiv 2026.03.13.26348306) automates mapping free-text TTE descriptions to Strategus JSON and executable R, improving shareable machine-readable specs for OHDSI-style studies; it does not compel release of rejected protocols or non-OMOP phenotype licenses. Scattered tutorials (e.g. Hoffman steroids-trial-emulation with simulated data) and TrialEmulation show that reference code can be released, which does not make re-runnable artifacts common for applied emulations on licensed claims/EHR. Queries run: TARGET reproducibility code phenotype; OHDSI Phenotype Library; THESEUS Strategus TTE; STaRT-RWE HARPER code sharing; RECORD-PE STROBE rejected protocol versions. No 2025–2026 guidance requires publishing rejected protocol versions or institution-exportable simulated test datasets as the standard companion to TARGET. Legal and data-model barriers named in the problem remain. Partial solve for OHDSI-adjacent machine-readable design; field-wide unavailability of code, full phenotypes, weight diagnostics, and rejected versions remains open. Cites 10.1001/jama.2025.13350: Does not resolve executable reproducibility; establishes the reporting standard the claim correctly distinguishes from code, phenotype, and rejected-protocol release. Included as the cited prior work that frames what remains out of scope.. Cites ohdsi/PhenotypeLibrary: Partial infrastructure for publishing complete phenotype logic with versioning and DOIs inside the OMOP/OHDSI ecosystem, addressing one stated blocker (code lists and versions) for studies that use that stack.. Cites 10.64898/2026.03.13.26348306: Shows LLM-assisted standardization of TTE design text into constrained JSON and executable Strategus R scripts, improving machine-readable, shareable analysis specs in OHDSI settings; proposal/automation of the coding step rather than field-wide release of phenotypes, weight diagnostics, or rejected protocols..

glm

open / supported-with-caveat. The claim is largely coherent and the reasons given (licensing constraints, institutional tooling embedding phenotype logic, unrunnable released code, nobody keeping rejected protocols) are practical barriers that support the claim being open as a matter of current practice. However, the phrasing ‘not available for emulations’ could be read as universal—no emulation anywhere publishes these materials—when the intended meaning is clearly ‘not routinely or standardly available.’ The statement’s own language (‘What remains unavailable in practice’) mitigates this, but the title-level claim is slightly broader than the evidence supports. The claim correctly distinguishes the TARGET statement as a transparency instrument rather than a risk-of-bias tool, and correctly identifies that faithful protocol reporting in prose does not guarantee operative reproducibility when decisions are expressed in code. The reasons given are about current practice wearing the language of a gap, not structural impossibility, which is the right framing. The severity is proportionate: irreproducible emulations carry real costs for decision-makers who cannot verify or re-run analyses.

Decision path

title: Variance estimation after cloning and sequence expansion has no scalable, correct default
text: SFW-01 Unverifiable High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Variance estimation after cloning and sequence expansion has no scalable, correct default
text:
Statement
Sequential emulation and cloning expand a dataset by orders of magnitude: a row per eligible decision point per person, multiplied by the strategies each person is initially compatible with. Two dependence structures result, repeated participation and clone-level copies of one history, and naive standard errors ignore both. Person-clustered sandwich inference handles both scalably when the weights are treated as fixed or the estimating-equation conditions hold, and for parametric marginal structural models with inverse probability weighting there are now evaluated alternatives with simulation guidance on coverage against cost. No default handles the harder case: clone-level dependence together with site clustering and the uncertainty from weights estimated by flexible nuisance models, at sequence-expansion scale. The bootstrap that would is correct in principle and prohibitive in practice once nuisance models must be refitted per replicate.

title: Variance estimation after cloning and sequence expansion has no scalable, correct default
text:
Why it is open
The dependence is nested and partly induced by the analysis rather than present in the data, so the clustering variable that is correct for repeated participation is not obviously correct for clones. An influence-function variance estimator needs the influence function of the full estimator including the weight-estimation step, which is unavailable in closed form once the nuisance models are learned. Every workaround trades in the same currency: subsampling to make the bootstrap affordable reintroduces the finite-sample instability the bootstrap was there to characterize.

title: Variance estimation after cloning and sequence expansion has no scalable, correct default
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Su L, et al. TrialEmulation: an R package to emulate target trials for causal analysis of observational time-to-event data. arXiv 2024
Implements sequence expansion, censoring-weight calculation and outcome models for intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses, with chunked processing for the data expansion.


TrialEmulation getting-started vignette
Documents the all-in-one initiators() workflow and the modular functions, which is the reference implementation practitioners actually use.

title: Variance estimation after cloning and sequence expansion has no scalable, correct default
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use person-clustered sandwich inference as the default where its conditions hold, and state that the weights were treated as fixed when they were. Derive a variance estimator that propagates estimated-weight and flexible-nuisance uncertainty and accommodates site-level sampling, which is the case no current option covers, and check its coverage against a person-level bootstrap on data small enough to run both. Support the scale with streaming risk-set construction, columnar back ends and case-control sampling with proven error control rather than heuristic subsampling.

title: Variance estimation after cloning and sequence expansion has no scalable, correct default
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source said. “Sequential emulation and cloning expand a dataset by orders of magnitude: each person contributes a row per eligible decision point, and cloning multiplies that by the number of strategies with which the person is initially compatible. Two dependence structures result. Repeated eligibility means a person appears in many trials, and cloning means several rows are copies of the same person’s history. Naive standard errors ignore both. The bootstrap is correct in principle and often prohibitive at this scale, particularly with flexible nuisance models that must be refitted per replicate. The TrialEmulation package supports sequence expansion, censoring weights, outcome models and chunked processing, and general scalable variance estimation for this design remains unsettled.”
What was wrong with it. Person-clustered sandwich inference is a scalable answer to the dependence created by repeated eligibility and cloning when the weights are fixed or the estimating-equation conditions hold, and evaluated options now exist for the parametric case with inverse probability weighting. The entry treated the whole problem as unsettled. What remains unsettled is narrower and still real.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported-with-caveat): The variance problem for the sequence-expansion half of this entry has been addressed: a 2025 paper compares sandwich, nonparametric bootstrap, jackknife and linearized estimating function bootstrap confidence intervals for sequential trial emulation with survival outcomes and finds a computationally feasible option with better coverage in the motivating regime. The entry should not present that as open. The cloning half is not covered by that work, and a search for variance estimation under cloning specifically returned nothing, so the dependence induced by copies of the same person remains unaddressed. The computational directions the entry proposes, streaming risk sets and columnar back ends, appear nowhere in the corpus. codex dissented (overstated): The full-estimator variance problem remains real, but the stated rationale overreaches. Rows created by repeated eligibility or cloning remain within the original individual, so clustering on that individual handles arbitrary dependence among those rows; clone dependence is not a separate sampling level. The pinned TrialEmulation source automatically computes a person-clustered sandwich covariance for its fitted MSM, providing a scalable analytic default for the outcome-model estimating equation. It does not propagate uncertainty from estimated switching or censoring weights, flexible nuisance learning, or site-level sampling. If sites are the independent units, inference should generally cluster or resample sites rather than treat clones-within-person-within-site as an exotic multiway structure. Likewise, a bootstrap is valid only when it resamples the appropriate independent unit and refits the full pipeline. A learner-specific closed-form influence function is also not universally necessary for orthogonal, cross-fitted estimators under suitable rate conditions. grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): Inverted prior: assume scalable correct variance already exists. Highest-yield hit is Limozin, Seaman, and Su (SMMR 2025; arXiv 2407.08317), co-authored with the TrialEmulation lead: they compare sandwich, nonparametric bootstrap, jackknife, and a new LEF bootstrap for sequential trial emulation (STE) marginal risk differences under IPW. LEF is faster than full bootstrap and covers better under the sparse regimes that motivate STE; sandwich is fastest and covers well only with large n and medium/high event rates. They state explicitly that sandwich is the only CI method in TrialEmulation and that it ignores weight-estimation uncertainty. That is real progress on the sequential-eligibility half of the claim.
It does not close the problem as stated. Coverage guidance is setting-specific, not a single default. LEF is research code (GitHub simulation repo), not a TrialEmulation default. The design is parametric MSM/IPW STE, not nested clone-within-person-within-site dependence from multi-strategy cloning, and not influence functions for flexible nuisance models. Clone-censor-weight primers (Gaber et al. 2024; Webster-Clark et al. PDS 2025; survivalCCW) still recommend bootstrap or robust SE and ship bootstrap vignettes; they do not deliver streaming IF or Arrow/DuckDB risk-set variance. Queries run: sequential trial variance sandwich bootstrap jackknife; clone-censor-weight variance; TrialEmulation robust SE; arXiv 2407.08317; survivalCCW; Enders 2018 sandwich (still not off-the-shelf). No 2025–2026 package release supplies a general scalable correct default for both cloning and sequence expansion under flexible nuisances. Partial solve of STE inference guidance; core gap remains.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The variance problem for the sequence-expansion half of this entry has been addressed: a 2025 paper compares sandwich, nonparametric bootstrap, jackknife and linearized estimating function bootstrap confidence intervals for sequential trial emulation with survival outcomes and finds a computationally feasible option with better coverage in the motivating regime. The entry should not present that as open. The cloning half is not covered by that work, and a search for variance estimation under cloning specifically returned nothing, so the dependence induced by copies of the same person remains unaddressed. The computational directions the entry proposes, streaming risk sets and columnar back ends, appear nowhere in the corpus. Cites 10.1177/09622802251356594: Supplies and evaluates variance estimation for sequence expansion, including a bootstrap alternative fast enough to run..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. The full-estimator variance problem remains real, but the stated rationale overreaches. Rows created by repeated eligibility or cloning remain within the original individual, so clustering on that individual handles arbitrary dependence among those rows; clone dependence is not a separate sampling level. The pinned TrialEmulation source automatically computes a person-clustered sandwich covariance for its fitted MSM, providing a scalable analytic default for the outcome-model estimating equation. It does not propagate uncertainty from estimated switching or censoring weights, flexible nuisance learning, or site-level sampling. If sites are the independent units, inference should generally cluster or resample sites rather than treat clones-within-person-within-site as an exotic multiway structure. Likewise, a bootstrap is valid only when it resamples the appropriate independent unit and refits the full pipeline. A learner-specific closed-form influence function is also not universally necessary for orthogonal, cross-fitted estimators under suitable rate conditions. Cites CRAN package TrialEmulation 0.0.4.11: The NAMESPACE exports trial_msm, and the pinned implementation automatically invokes robust_calculation with the original individual identifier. robust_calculation uses sandwich::vcovCL clustered by that identifier. This resolves the duplication-induced within-person component, but not full nuisance-estimation or site-level uncertainty..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Inverted prior: assume scalable correct variance already exists. Highest-yield hit is Limozin, Seaman, and Su (SMMR 2025; arXiv 2407.08317), co-authored with the TrialEmulation lead: they compare sandwich, nonparametric bootstrap, jackknife, and a new LEF bootstrap for sequential trial emulation (STE) marginal risk differences under IPW. LEF is faster than full bootstrap and covers better under the sparse regimes that motivate STE; sandwich is fastest and covers well only with large n and medium/high event rates. They state explicitly that sandwich is the only CI method in TrialEmulation and that it ignores weight-estimation uncertainty. That is real progress on the sequential-eligibility half of the claim.


It does not close the problem as stated. Coverage guidance is setting-specific, not a single default. LEF is research code (GitHub simulation repo), not a TrialEmulation default. The design is parametric MSM/IPW STE, not nested clone-within-person-within-site dependence from multi-strategy cloning, and not influence functions for flexible nuisance models. Clone-censor-weight primers (Gaber et al. 2024; Webster-Clark et al. PDS 2025; survivalCCW) still recommend bootstrap or robust SE and ship bootstrap vignettes; they do not deliver streaming IF or Arrow/DuckDB risk-set variance. Queries run: sequential trial variance sandwich bootstrap jackknife; clone-censor-weight variance; TrialEmulation robust SE; arXiv 2407.08317; survivalCCW; Enders 2018 sandwich (still not off-the-shelf). No 2025–2026 package release supplies a general scalable correct default for both cloning and sequence expansion under flexible nuisances. Partial solve of STE inference guidance; core gap remains. Cites 10.1177/09622802251356594: Provides a full simulation comparison of sandwich, nonparametric bootstrap, LEF bootstrap, and jackknife for STE marginal risk differences; adapts LEF bootstrap to STE; documents that TrialEmulation implements only sandwich and that sandwich ignores weight uncertainty; gives practical choice rules by sample size and event rate.. Cites arxiv:2407.08317: Open preprint of the same STE inference comparison; confirms dependence induced by patients entering multiple trials and the computational barrier of nonparametric bootstrap.. Cites 10.1007/s40471-024-00346-2: Does not solve scalable variance; documents current practice that CCW inference requires bootstrap or robust variance, reinforcing that a correct cloning-aware default is still an implementation gap rather than a solved product feature..

glm

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and proportionate. It does not assert impossibility; it says the problem ‘remains unsettled,’ which is a claim about the state of methodology and practice. The reason given for openness—nested dependence (clones within persons within sites) and the lack of closed-form influence functions once nuisance models are learned—is a genuine methodological gap that structurally supports the claim being open. The acknowledgment that the bootstrap is ‘correct in principle’ but ‘often prohibitive’ is a fair characterization of a practical tradeoff rather than an overstatement. I cannot verify what the TrialEmulation package does or does not implement, but the core methodological claim about the absence of a scalable, correct default variance estimator for this design is coherent and the stated reasons entail openness. The claim about software capabilities is not the load-bearing part of the argument; the load-bearing part is the identifiability/derivability of the influence function under learned nuisance models, which is a methodological claim I can assess for coherence.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=3/4) → R7:counter-and-support-both-present(support=1/counter=1)

title: Calling an analysis a target trial emulation is treated as evidence about its assumption burden
text: REG-03 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 5/5

title: Calling an analysis a target trial emulation is treated as evidence about its assumption burden
text:
Statement
Target trial specification improves temporal alignment, protocol clarity and estimand definition. It does not establish consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity, valid measurement, correct estimation or transportability, and those are separate conditions rather than steps on one scale: any of them can hold while the others fail. In practice the label does the work of all of them. An analysis that adopts the framework is read as though the whole set had been secured, and no convention asks a study to state the six requirements separately for the estimand it chose. The reporting evidence shows how weakly the label constrains the practice: of 200 published studies claiming to emulate a trial, 43% did not describe all key emulation components.

title: Calling an analysis a target trial emulation is treated as evidence about its assumption burden
text:
Why it is open
The framework’s value is real, which is what makes the substitution durable: naming the target trial does prevent a class of self-inflicted biases, so the label is informative and is then over-read. Stating the requirements separately needs a vocabulary that does not exist in usable form, so an author wishing to be precise has to invent the terms. Reviewers and editors also use the label as a screening heuristic, which rewards using it and penalizes qualifying it.

title: Calling an analysis a target trial emulation is treated as evidence about its assumption burden
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Hubbard RA, Hernán MA. “Target trial emulation” for observational studies: potential and pitfalls. N Engl J Med 2024
States what emulation does and does not secure, which is exactly the distinction the label erases in use.


Hansford HJ, et al. Reporting of observational studies explicitly aiming to emulate randomized trials: a systematic review. JAMA Netw Open 2023
Finds that 43% of 200 studies claiming to emulate a trial did not describe all key emulation components, which measures how weakly the label constrains the practice.

title: Calling an analysis a target trial emulation is treated as evidence about its assumption burden
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Require every emulation to state the six requirements separately for its chosen estimand, saying which are argued, which are assumed and which are diagnosed, rather than claiming a single level of credibility. Have journals ask for that statement instead of for the label, so adopting the framework is reported as a design fact and credibility is argued on its own. Audit a sample of published emulations against the six requirements to establish the current distribution, since nobody presently knows how many are argued at all.

title: Calling an analysis a target trial emulation is treated as evidence about its assumption burden
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “The assumptions an analysis needs form a ladder, and each step up adds one: from describing an association, to adjusting for measured confounders, to identifying a sustained-strategy effect, to transporting that effect to another population. A paper should identify the highest step its evidence plausibly reaches. In practice the label target trial emulation is doing that work instead: an analysis that adopts the framework is read as though it had climbed the ladder, when the framework secures the temporal alignment and nothing above it. The label has become a claim about credibility rather than a description of a design, and no convention exists for stating which step a given study actually reaches.”
What was wrong with it. The ladder metaphor implies a single ordered scale, and the requirements are not ordered: consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity, valid measurement, correct estimation and transportability are separate conditions that can hold or fail independently. A study should state them separately for its chosen estimand rather than claim a rung.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): The corpus shows the label spreading rapidly across clinical specialties, with comprehensive analyses of emulation practice in oncology and reviews in neurology, multiple sclerosis and military medicine, and it contains no published ladder of assumption levels with named rungs, and no study stating which rung its evidence reaches. The reporting review’s finding that 43% of studies claiming to emulate a trial did not describe all key components is direct evidence that the label constrains practice weakly, which is the entry’s central claim.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. The corpus shows the label spreading rapidly across clinical specialties, with comprehensive analyses of emulation practice in oncology and reviews in neurology, multiple sclerosis and military medicine, and it contains no published ladder of assumption levels with named rungs, and no study stating which rung its evidence reaches. The reporting review’s finding that 43% of studies claiming to emulate a trial did not describe all key components is direct evidence that the label constrains practice weakly, which is the entry’s central claim. Cites 10.1093/oncolo/oyag258: Documents how widely the label is applied in one specialty and how variably the underlying design is executed.. Cites 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.36023: Quantifies the gap between claiming the framework and reporting its components..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The underlying risk is real: naming a target trial does not establish causal identification. The proposed ladder is technically wrong, however, because the requirements are not nested one assumption at a time. Sustained strategies require history-specific consistency, sequential exchangeability, and sequential positivity, while transportability adds distinct population-exchangeability and support conditions. Target trial specification also contributes more than temporal alignment by defining the estimand and protocol components, although it guarantees none of those assumptions. The issue is critical only when the label substitutes for an explicit identification argument.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. The claim is that the label target trial emulation is used as a credibility credential rather than as a design description of temporal alignment and protocol specification, and that no shared vocabulary states which step on an assumption-to-conclusion ladder a study reaches. Literature search under the inverted prior found restatements and measurements of this problem, not a solved convention. Hubbard and Hernán (N Engl J Med 2024) state what emulation does and does not secure, call sensitivity analysis for unobserved confounding essential, and explicitly deny that the framework is a panacea; that strengthens the conceptual distinction the problem describes and does not install a journal-level rung vocabulary or stop label-as-credibility use. Hansford et al. JAMA Netw Open 2023 quantifies weak adherence among studies that claim to emulate a trial (large fractions missing key components or dual protocol/emulation description), which shows the label does not bind practice. TARGET (2025) improves transparent reporting of the emulation claim and assumptions but does not replace the label with a required statement of the highest justified causal step, nor invent named intermediate rungs from association through measured confounding, sustained strategies, and transport. No 2024–2026 journal policy or reporting addendum was found that requires authors to declare an assumption ladder rung instead of (or in addition to) the TTE label, and no widely adopted named vocabulary for intermediate rungs was located. Commentaries that warn against over-reading TTE as causal certification reinforce that the misuse remains live. Proposal-stage ladders outside TTE (generic credibility ladders in other fields) do not solve the emulation-label problem as stated. Queries included: TTE label overused credibility; assumption ladder target trial; journal policy require emulation components 2024–2026; Hubbard Hernán potential pitfalls follow-on; TARGET vs causal claim strength.

glm

abstain / supported. The claim is internally consistent and proportionate. It describes a sociological dynamic where the TTE label substitutes for explicit assumption-burden statements. The rationale correctly identifies the structural reasons this persists (lack of vocabulary for intermediate rungs, institutional incentives). This is a claim about current practice. I abstain on the status axis because verifying reviewer and editor practices requires evidence I cannot reach.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: Regulators have no thresholds for adequate emulation, acceptable residual confounding or sufficient sensitivity analysis
text: REG-01 Confirmed open High priority Promising Tractability 3/5

title: Regulators have no thresholds for adequate emulation, acceptable residual confounding or sufficient sensitivity analysis
text:
Statement
FDA guidance asks sponsors to describe an approach that supports causal inference and names target trial emulation where appropriate. NICE states that some target trials cannot be adequately emulated and that bespoke data collection may then be preferable. EMA and ICH guidance emphasize fit-for-use data, prespecification and transparent non-interventional design. None supplies an acceptance criterion, and a universal numerical cutoff for emulation adequacy, residual confounding or sensitivity-analysis sufficiency would not be technically defensible if one were offered. What is missing is the defensible version: prespecified, decision-specific criteria covering protocol fidelity, identification plausibility, data fitness, diagnostics, quantitative bias analysis and robustness of the decision itself, agreed before the submission rather than argued after it. Sponsors therefore cannot know in advance whether a submission will be accepted, and reviewers have no consistent basis to accept or reject one.

title: Regulators have no thresholds for adequate emulation, acceptable residual confounding or sufficient sensitivity analysis
text:
Why it is open
The quantities that would be thresholded, residual confounding and estimand distance, are not identified from the data of the study in question, so any fixed cutoff would be applied to an unmeasurable object. A criterion has to be decision-specific because the tolerable bias depends on what the decision costs, which means the work is to build a family of criteria rather than a number. Agencies are also reasoning from a small and non-random set of precedents, so the empirical base for calibrating even a decision-specific criterion does not yet exist.

title: Regulators have no thresholds for adequate emulation, acceptable residual confounding or sufficient sensitivity analysis
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




FDA guidance on non-interventional studies for drug and biological products
Asks sponsors to describe an approach supporting causal inference, naming target trial emulation where appropriate, without setting an acceptance threshold.


NICE real-world evidence framework
Recognizes that some target trials cannot be adequately emulated and may require bespoke data collection, which is the closest any guidance comes to a stop rule.


ICH E9(R1) addendum on estimands and sensitivity analysis in clinical trials
Establishes the estimand framework and the requirement for aligned sensitivity analyses, which regulators apply to trials and have not translated into thresholds for emulations.

title: Regulators have no thresholds for adequate emulation, acceptable residual confounding or sufficient sensitivity analysis
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build regulator-facing evidence dossiers that separate protocol fidelity, identification assumptions, data validation, diagnostics and decision robustness into distinct sections, so a reviewer can accept some and reject others rather than judging the whole. Develop prespecified, decision-specific acceptance criteria rather than universal cutoffs, agreed with the reviewer before the analysis. Conduct prospective qualification studies of data sources and phenotypes, and treat randomized-trial benchmarking as one input to calibration rather than the sole route to it, since the benchmarking corpus is a selected sample of emulable questions.

title: Regulators have no thresholds for adequate emulation, acceptable residual confounding or sufficient sensitivity analysis
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “FDA guidance asks sponsors to describe an approach that supports causal inference and names target trial emulation where appropriate. NICE states that some target trials cannot be adequately emulated and that bespoke data collection may then be preferable. EMA and ICH guidance emphasize fit-for-use data, prespecification and transparent non-interventional design. What none of them supplies is a threshold: how close an emulation must be to count as adequate, how much residual confounding is acceptable for a given decision, or what set of sensitivity analyses is sufficient. Sponsors therefore cannot know in advance whether a submission will be accepted, and reviewers have no consistent basis on which to accept or reject one.”
What was wrong with it. The entry treated the absent thresholds as a gap to be filled. Universal numerical cutoffs for emulation adequacy, residual confounding and sensitivity-analysis sufficiency are not technically defensible, so their absence is partly correct rather than wholly a failure. The unmet need is prespecified, decision-specific criteria rather than universal ones, and benchmarking against randomized trials is supporting evidence rather than the only route to evaluation.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): The corpus contains regulatory and decision-facing syntheses for oncology, cardiology devices and GLP-1 therapies, all of which describe considerations rather than thresholds. A 2026 Journal of Clinical Oncology paper addresses emulation for regulatory and clinical decision making in cancer without setting an acceptance criterion. This is consistent with the entry: guidance exists, thresholds do not, and the reason given by the entry, that the quantities that would be thresholded are not identified from the study’s own data, is a structural reason rather than an oversight.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. The corpus contains regulatory and decision-facing syntheses for oncology, cardiology devices and GLP-1 therapies, all of which describe considerations rather than thresholds. A 2026 Journal of Clinical Oncology paper addresses emulation for regulatory and clinical decision making in cancer without setting an acceptance criterion. This is consistent with the entry: guidance exists, thresholds do not, and the reason given by the entry, that the quantities that would be thresholded are not identified from the study’s own data, is a structural reason rather than an oversight. Cites 10.1200/jco-25-01906: Addresses the decision-facing use of emulation directly, and describes considerations rather than acceptance thresholds..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

Residual confounding is generally unidentified without additional information, and acceptable bias depends on the estimand, decision loss, and uncertainty. Nevertheless, lacking a universal cutoff does not leave reviewers without a principled basis, and trial benchmarking cannot uniquely validate an emulation because agreement may reflect estimand differences, sampling error, or offsetting biases. Decision-specific tolerances, quantitative bias analysis, data validation, and prespecified diagnostics provide other bases for assessment.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Inverted-prior search for regulatory acceptance thresholds on emulation adequacy, residual confounding, or sufficient sensitivity analysis did not find any. The problem’s own cited instruments still describe process and design expectations without numeric or decision-rule cutoffs. FDA July 2024 final guidance on EHR and claims data (and related non-interventional RWE guidance) recommends quantitative bias analysis for misclassification and reliability issues, fitness-for-use assessment, and transparent causal design including target trial emulation where appropriate, but does not state how close an emulation must be, how large residual confounding may be, or which sensitivity package is enough for acceptance. NICE’s RWE framework explicitly treats some target trials as not adequately emulable and prefers bespoke collection in those cases; secondary commentary on the final framework notes that NICE deliberately does not set minimum acceptable quality standards. EMA’s March 2025 reflection paper on RWD in non-interventional studies for regulatory purposes (EMA/99865/2025) endorses target trial emulation for causal objectives, ICH E9(R1)-aligned sensitivity analysis, and case-by-case relevance determination; it does not supply thresholds. ICH E9(R1) remains a trial estimand and sensitivity framework, not a translation into emulation acceptance rules. Adjacent methods work (E-values, tipping-point and quantitative bias analysis, Faries et al. 2025 good practices for robustness of observational evidence) equip sponsors to quantify bias under assumed parameters; that is not a regulator-issued decision threshold, and any fixed numeric bar would still be decision-dependent as the report states. No 2024–2026 FDA, EMA, HMA, ICH, NICE, Health Canada, CDA-AMC, or ENCePP instrument located here closes the gap. Queries included: FDA/NICE/EMA residual confounding threshold and acceptance criteria; quantitative bias analysis regulatory threshold; ICH E9(R1) observational thresholds; ENCePP/DARWIN acceptance criteria 2025–2026; plus review of the three cited guidance PDFs and the 2025 EMA reflection paper.

glm

abstain / supported. The claim is internally consistent and proportionate. It asserts a current practice gap (no thresholds in guidance) and the rationale correctly identifies the structural barriers to creating such thresholds (metrics not identified from study data, gaming risk, decision-dependence of tolerable bias). This is a claim about current practice wearing the language of impossibility (‘cannot know in advance’). The scope is appropriate. I abstain on the status axis because verifying the content of the cited regulatory guidance is outside my reach.
