title: An unobservable protocol component produces a different, data-defined estimand rather than a noisy version of the intended one
text: PRO-04 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: An unobservable protocol component produces a different, data-defined estimand rather than a noisy version of the intended one
text:
Statement
The canonical protocol has seven linked components: eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment, follow-up, outcomes, causal contrast and analysis plan. Conceptual specification and operational realization are distinct, and when a component cannot be observed the analyst substitutes a proxy. If no valid measurement, missing-data or validation model recovers the intended variable, the resulting observed-data functional generally does not identify the intended causal effect, and it does not automatically identify some other one either: naming it a different estimand requires a corresponding intervention and an identification argument. A criterion that cannot be verified is dropped and the population changes; a strategy that cannot be distinguished from its neighbor is merged and the contrast changes; an outcome that is only partly captured redefines the endpoint. Nothing in current reporting requires the operational target and its assumptions to be stated, so the paper names the intended estimand and reports a functional whose causal interpretation was never argued.

title: An unobservable protocol component produces a different, data-defined estimand rather than a noisy version of the intended one
text:
Why it is open
The substitution happens component by component during implementation, often in code rather than in prose, and by the time results exist there is no artifact recording which component was compromised. Stating the operational target requires a language for partially specified interventions that does not yet exist in usable form. There is also a reasonable disagreement underneath: some substitutions are innocuous refinements and others change the question, and no criterion separates them.

title: An unobservable protocol component produces a different, data-defined estimand rather than a noisy version of the intended one
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Hernán MA, Robins JM. Using big data to emulate a target trial when a randomized trial is not available. Am J Epidemiol 2016;183(8):758-764
Establishes the seven components and the requirement to map each to the data, which is the framework within which the substitution becomes visible.


Moreno-Betancur M, et al. The ideal trial: defining causal estimands that balance relevance and feasibility in target trial emulations and actual randomized trials. arXiv 2024
Argues that discrepancies between the ideal, target and actual trials should be made explicit, which is the general case of this specific substitution.


Wang, et al. An operational target trial emulation framework for causal inference using electronic health records. npj Digit Med 2026
Works through the operational realization of each component against record data, which is where the substitutions occur in practice.

title: An unobservable protocol component produces a different, data-defined estimand rather than a noisy version of the intended one
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Require a component-by-component mapping table carrying each component’s conceptual specification, its operational realization, and what changed between them. Where a component cannot be realized, require the operational target and its assumptions to be stated, without labeling it a causal estimand unless an intervention and an identification argument are supplied. Develop criteria, tested against benchmarking data, for which substitutions historically preserved agreement with the corresponding trial and which did not.

title: An unobservable protocol component produces a different, data-defined estimand rather than a noisy version of the intended one
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “The canonical protocol has seven linked components: eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment, follow-up, outcomes, causal contrast and analysis plan. Conceptual specification and operational realization are distinct, and when a required component cannot be observed the analyst does not obtain a mismeasured version of the intended effect. They obtain a different effect, defined by what the data can express. A criterion that cannot be verified is dropped and the population changes; a strategy that cannot be distinguished from its neighbor is merged and the contrast changes; an outcome that is only partly captured redefines the endpoint. Nothing in current reporting requires that substitution to be named, so the paper states the intended estimand and reports the substituted one.”
What was wrong with it. Calling the result a substituted causal estimand was too strong. When an intended protocol variable is replaced by an operational proxy and no valid measurement, missing-data or validation model recovers the intended variable, the resulting observed-data functional generally does not identify the intended effect and need not identify any well-defined causal effect. Naming it an estimand requires a corresponding intervention and an identification argument, which the substitution does not supply.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): Operational frameworks for mapping each protocol component onto record data exist, and a 2024 Frontiers in Pharmacology case study applies the estimand and target trial frameworks together to an external control analysis, which is the closest the corpus comes to naming the substituted estimand explicitly. None requires that the substituted estimand replace the intended one in the paper’s headline, and none supplies criteria for which substitutions preserve the question. The entry’s claim is about a reporting requirement rather than a method, and no such requirement appears in the reporting literature.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. Operational frameworks for mapping each protocol component onto record data exist, and a 2024 Frontiers in Pharmacology case study applies the estimand and target trial frameworks together to an external control analysis, which is the closest the corpus comes to naming the substituted estimand explicitly. None requires that the substituted estimand replace the intended one in the paper’s headline, and none supplies criteria for which substitutions preserve the question. The entry’s claim is about a reporting requirement rather than a method, and no such requirement appears in the reporting literature. Cites 10.3389/fphar.2024.1223858: Combines the estimand framework with the target trial framework so the realized estimand is stated, which is the practice the entry asks to be made general.. Cites 10.1038/s41746-026-02563-z: Works through the operational realization of each component, which is where substitutions occur..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The statement treats all failures of observation as estimand substitution, which is incorrect. Depending on the measurement and identification structure, an operational proxy may still identify the intended effect through a valid measurement-error, missing-data, or validation model; it may define a different, well-defined causal effect; or it may identify only a statistical functional with no coherent intervention-based interpretation. Dropping an eligibility criterion, merging strategies, and redefining an endpoint change the target only when the analyst actually makes those substitutions. They are not logically forced by partial observation. Conversely, simply naming a substituted estimand does not make it causal or identified. Agreement with a benchmark trial cannot determine whether an estimand was preserved because different targets and compensating biases can yield similar estimates. Component-level conceptual-to-operational mapping is important and can be decision-critical, but the universal claim and very-high-severity framing are excessive.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Conceptual naming of substituted estimands is advanced by Moreno-Betancur ideal/target/actual trials and by operational TTE frameworks (Hernán–Robins components; Wang npj Digit Med 2026 operational EHR mapping). That is partial progress on making substitution visible. Missing pieces remain: a usable language for partially specified interventions, mandatory component-by-component conceptual vs operational tables with substituted estimand as headline, and criteria validated on benchmarking data for which substitutions preserve trial agreement. Not fully solved. Cites arXiv:2405.10026: Partial: explicit ideal vs target vs actual trial discrepancies so unobservable components can be named as changed estimands rather than measurement error; does not deliver component mapping tables, partial-intervention language, or benchmarking criteria for innocuous vs question-changing substitutions.. Cites 10.1038/s41746-026-02563-z: Partial: works through operational realization of protocol components against EHR data, the setting where component substitution occurs; does not require substituted estimands as headline quantities or validation criteria for which substitutions preserve trial agreement..

glm

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and pitched at the right level of generality. It argues that an unobservable protocol component produces a different estimand rather than a noisy version, and that current reporting does not require naming this substitution. The reason given—that the substitution happens in code, no artifact records it, and no usable language or criterion currently exists to separate innocuous from question-changing substitutions—supports the claim that this remains an open gap in practice.

title: Inference conditions on a fixed target trial that was in fact selected after seeing the data
text: PRO-02 Partially addressed High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: Inference conditions on a fixed target trial that was in fact selected after seeing the data
text:
Statement
Eligibility thresholds, comparators, grace periods, washout windows and outcome definitions are routinely revised after investigators inspect the data. When outcome-relevant information from the analysis data is used to select among candidate protocols, a confidence interval calibrated for a protocol fixed in advance need not have nominal coverage for the selected estimand, unless the selection is incorporated into the inference or separated out through independent data. Saying so requires naming the target of inference and whether the coverage claimed is conditional on the selection or marginal over it, and applied reports do neither. Design multiverse analyses of emulations exist and display the spread of estimates across specifications, which is informative and is not a correction: a multiverse shows the sensitivity and leaves the reported interval uncalibrated for the search that produced it.

title: Inference conditions on a fixed target trial that was in fact selected after seeing the data
text:
Why it is open
The search is usually undocumented, so even a method that corrected for it would have no record of what was searched. Selective-inference corrections exist for well-defined selection events such as variable selection under a known rule, and protocol development is not one: it is a sequence of human decisions with no likelihood. Splitting the data into design and analysis halves solves the inference problem and costs precision in exactly the settings, rare treatments and rare outcomes, where precision is already binding.

title: Inference conditions on a fixed target trial that was in fact selected after seeing the data
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Hansford HJ, et al. Design and implementation of observational studies emulating a target trial. JAMA Netw Open 2026
Enumerates the design decisions an emulation must make, which is also the enumeration of what can be revised after seeing data.


Hansford HJ, Cashin AG, Jones MD, et al. Transparent reporting of observational studies emulating a target trial: the TARGET statement. JAMA 2025
A 21-item reporting checklist for the final specification. Its purpose is transparency about what was done, not a record of what was rejected.

title: Inference conditions on a fixed target trial that was in fact selected after seeing the data
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Divide the data into a design partition and an analysis partition, or expose only outcome-blinded metadata during protocol development, so the search happens where it cannot contaminate inference. Where a selection-aware correction is attempted, state the target of inference and whether coverage is conditional or marginal, since the claim is not well formed without it. Require dated decision logs so the search becomes a recorded object: a correction is impossible while the search history is unavailable even to the investigators.

title: Inference conditions on a fixed target trial that was in fact selected after seeing the data
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Eligibility thresholds, comparators, grace periods, washout windows and outcome definitions are routinely revised after investigators inspect the data. Even an investigator who never looks at a treatment effect can be influenced by outcome prevalence, by covariate-outcome associations or by which specification yields a workable sample size. Standard inferential theory conditions on a fixed target trial and takes no account of the search over candidate emulations that produced it, so the reported confidence interval has the wrong coverage for the procedure actually run. A protocol chosen by an algorithm is an estimated object with its own sampling variability, and nothing in current practice treats it as one.”
What was wrong with it. The coverage claim needs its condition stated. An interval calibrated for a protocol fixed in advance loses nominal coverage when outcome-relevant information from the analysis data is used to select among protocols, and the statement has to name which target of inference and which coverage probability, conditional or marginal, is meant. Design multiverse analyses of emulations also already exist, which the entry did not acknowledge.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The entry says standard inference conditions on a fixed target trial and ignores the search over candidate emulations. The search is now being reported in at least one applied setting: a 2025 European Journal of Epidemiology study uses a multiverse analysis to characterize uncertainty in the estimated effect of statin initiation on dementia across design choices. That is the design multiverse the entry proposes, already run. What remains unaddressed is the inferential half: a multiverse displays the spread and does not correct coverage, and no selective-inference treatment of protocol selection exists in the corpus. The entry should not claim the multiverse is absent. Cites 10.1007/s10654-025-01231-y: Runs the design multiverse the entry proposes, in an applied emulation, which means the proposal has a precedent rather than being untried.. Cites 10.1093/aje/kwae346: Documents the specification choices oncology emulations actually make, which is the empirical base for describing the search space..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Outcome-dependent selection of a protocol using the analysis data can invalidate an interval calibrated for a protocol fixed in advance, so the narrowed problem is real. It is not true that every data-informed revision produces wrong coverage. Choices based only on treatment and covariate information may be handled conditionally, independent design and analysis samples break the relevant dependence, and simultaneous or selection-aware inference can cover specified searches. An algorithmically selected protocol produces a data-adaptive target; that does not automatically create an extra variance component, because coverage must first be defined conditionally or marginally and for either the selected estimand or a fixed scientific estimand. An undocumented human search precludes an exact reconstruction of that selection event, but it does not make all valid inference impossible. High severity is warranted only when outcome-relevant selection is material and ignored.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Selective-inference and post-selection literature exists for covariates and models, not for human search over TTE protocol components (eligibility, grace period, washout, outcomes). TARGET and Hansford 2025–2026 report the final protocol; they do not correct coverage for data-dependent protocol selection. Outcome-blinded design splits and dated decision logs remain proposals, not standard practice or validated TTE-specific selective-inference procedures. No CRAN/GitHub change for TrialEmulation/lmtp/ltmle/gfoRmula treats the protocol as a random object. Open.

glm

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and proportionate. It asserts that current practice does not treat the protocol as an estimated object with sampling variability. The reason given for it being open—that the search is undocumented and protocol development is not a well-defined selection event—directly supports the claim that standard inferential theory and current practice fail to account for this search. The scope is correctly pitched at current practice.

title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
text: OVL-01 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
text:
Statement
A deterministic treatment strategy can assign a treatment that clinicians almost never give to patients with certain covariate histories. The standard response is to inspect the weight distribution and truncate the tail. Truncation is bias-variance regularization: it cannot identify an effect where the treatment density is structurally zero, and a marginal weight summary does not say which intervention-relevant histories carry small or zero density. What a reader needs and does not get is a policy-specific support criterion fixed in advance, diagnostics localized by time and by history, the fraction of the target population that fails the criterion, and the estimand that survives once those strata are set aside. Empirically, poor overlap has been shown to defeat adjustment methods that were otherwise well specified, which is the failure a weight histogram is least able to show. Software for stochastic and modified treatment policies covers part of the continuous longitudinal case; partial-identification bounds for arbitrary sustained strategies do not exist.

title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
text:
Why it is open
Practical positivity is a property of a conditional density over a growing history, so beyond a few time points the object to be diagnosed is high-dimensional and cannot be plotted. Truncation is attractive precisely because it converts an identification failure into a variance reduction, which reads as a modeling improvement rather than as a change of question. Reporting an unsupported fraction also requires deciding what counts as support, and any such criterion is a decision about the estimand that nobody is currently required to state.

title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Target trial emulation under nonmutually exclusive assignment. Am J Epidemiol 2026;195(4):1045
Shows that poor overlap can defeat advanced adjustment methods, in a setting where assignment to strategies is not mutually exclusive.


lmtp: Non-Parametric Causal Effects of Feasible Interventions Based on Modified Treatment Policies. CRAN
Implements modified treatment policies and stochastic interventions for binary, categorical, continuous and multivariate treatments with censored outcomes and competing risks, which is the estimand class that restores positivity.

title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Prespecify a policy-specific support criterion, report time- and history-localized support diagnostics against it, and report the sensitivity of the conclusion to the criterion, so the definition is visible rather than implicit. Replace or restrict deterministic regimes the data cannot support with modified treatment policies, incremental propensity-score interventions or stochastic initiation rules where that is scientifically acceptable, and say so in the paper rather than in the truncation. Derive partial-identification bounds for the unsupported strata under sustained strategies, which is the piece no current software supplies.

title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “A deterministic treatment strategy can assign a treatment that clinicians almost never give to patients with certain covariate histories. The standard response is to inspect the weight distribution and truncate the tail, which reduces variance, changes the implicit estimand and can leave substantial bias in place. What the diagnostic does not report is the quantity a reader needs: what fraction of the target population has no support for the strategy under study, which histories are the unsupported ones, and what estimand remains identified once they are set aside. A 2026 study of non-mutually exclusive assignment found that poor overlap defeated adjustment methods that were otherwise well specified, which is the failure mode a weight histogram is least able to show.”
What was wrong with it. Truncation is bias-variance regularization and does not change the estimand in the way the entry implied; what it cannot do is identify an effect under structural nonpositivity. Software for stochastic and modified treatment policies also partly addresses the continuous longitudinal case, so the alternatives the entry proposes are not entirely unavailable.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): The entry’s core claim, that diagnostics describe weights rather than naming which histories are unsupported, holds against the corpus. Two pieces of work sharpen rather than resolve it. A 2025 study measures the impact of near-positivity violations on IPTW-estimated marginal structural survival models with time-dependent covariates, which supplies the consequence the entry asserts. A 2026 American Journal of Epidemiology paper on target trial emulation under non-mutually exclusive assignment sets out structural pitfalls and remedies for exactly the overlap failure the entry cites. Neither produces a causal support map over histories, an unsupported-fraction statistic, or partial-identification bounds for the unsupported strata, so the specific artifacts the entry says are missing are still missing. codex dissented (overstated): A marginal weight histogram cannot localize poor support to particular histories, and structural nonpositivity is a decision-grade identification failure. However, the report conflates structural nonpositivity, practical near-nonpositivity, and finite-sample instability. Weight truncation does not convert an identification failure into variance reduction or necessarily define a coherent alternative causal estimand. It changes the estimating functional and usually biases estimation of the stated target, while structural nonpositivity remains unidentified. The claim that the high-dimensional object cannot be plotted is also too absolute because reduced history-specific diagnostics are possible. Pinned CICI 1.0 is a direct partial counterexample: its NAMESPACE exports feasible, plot.feasible, and summary.feasible; feasible() estimates conditional treatment densities, returns per-observation feasible intervention values and low_matrix objects, and reports the proportion below its threshold by strategy and time. Its gformula accepts the resulting individual intervention matrices. This implementation is limited to continuous interventions and an analyst-chosen alpha threshold, does not provide general partial-identification bounds, and does not cover arbitrary binary or categorical sustained strategies. Its threshold implementation also normalizes densities using bin widths but calculates cumsum(sort(row)) without bin-width weighting, so the advertised probability-mass threshold is miscalibrated whenever bin widths differ from one. Later-time diagnostics are evaluated over observed histories, which need not equal the history distribution induced by the intervention. Pinned lmtp 1.5.4 implements longitudinal modified treatment policies and an ipsi policy factory, but such intervention classes do not automatically restore positivity; policy-specific absolute continuity remains necessary, and lmtp trims estimated density ratios by default. Very-high severity is warranted when the prespecified strategy materially lacks support, but a universal support map and bounds are roadmap extensions rather than requirements for every adequately supported analysis.

Literature and prior-art check

Two pieces of work sharpen rather than resolve it. A 2025 study measures the impact of near-positivity violations on IPTW-estimated marginal structural survival models with time-dependent covariates, which supplies the consequence the entry asserts. Neither produces a causal support map over histories, an unsupported-fraction statistic, or partial-identification bounds for the unsupported strata, so the specific artifacts the entry says are missing are still missing. Cites 10.1093/aje/kwag014: Names the structural pitfalls of overlapping assignment and proposes remedies, which is the setting in which the entry’s overlap failure was demonstrated.. Cites 10.1002/bimj.70093: Measures how near-positivity degrades weighted longitudinal survival estimation, supporting the entry’s premise that truncation does not rescue the estimate..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

However, the report conflates structural nonpositivity, practical near-nonpositivity, and finite-sample instability. Weight truncation does not convert an identification failure into variance reduction or necessarily define a coherent alternative causal estimand. It changes the estimating functional and usually biases estimation of the stated target, while structural nonpositivity remains unidentified. The claim that the high-dimensional object cannot be plotted is also too absolute because reduced history-specific diagnostics are possible. Pinned CICI 1.0 is a direct partial counterexample: its NAMESPACE exports feasible, plot.feasible, and summary.feasible; feasible() estimates conditional treatment densities, returns per-observation feasible intervention values and low_matrix objects, and reports the proportion below its threshold by strategy and time. Its gformula accepts the resulting individual intervention matrices. This implementation is limited to continuous interventions and an analyst-chosen alpha threshold, does not provide general partial-identification bounds, and does not cover arbitrary binary or categorical sustained strategies. Its threshold implementation also normalizes densities using bin widths but calculates cumsum(sort(row)) without bin-width weighting, so the advertised probability-mass threshold is miscalibrated whenever bin widths differ from one. Later-time diagnostics are evaluated over observed histories, which need not equal the history distribution induced by the intervention. Pinned lmtp 1.5.4 implements longitudinal modified treatment policies and an ipsi policy factory, but such intervention classes do not automatically restore positivity; policy-specific absolute continuity remains necessary, and lmtp trims estimated density ratios by default. Very-high severity is warranted when the prespecified strategy materially lacks support, but a universal support map and bounds are roadmap extensions rather than requirements for every adequately supported analysis. Cites CRAN:CICI@1.0: The exported feasible workflow estimates history-conditional treatment densities, constructs per-observation feasible alternatives, records low-density cells, and reports a strategy- and time-specific fraction classified as infeasible. This resolves the central diagnostic request for a limited continuous-treatment setting.. Cites CRAN:lmtp@1.5.4: The package supplies longitudinal TMLE and sequentially doubly robust estimators for modified treatment policies and exports an incremental probability-shift factory, partially implementing the proposed alternative-estimand direction. It does not itself guarantee positivity or provide the requested support map..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Inverted prior: treat the diagnostic gap as already closed, then check. The report’s own citations do not close it. Takayama (AJE 2026; 10.1093/aje/kwaf018) shows that poor overlap can defeat well-specified adjustment under non-mutually exclusive assignment; that is evidence the failure mode is real, not a fix for naming unsupported histories. lmtp implements modified treatment policies (MTPs) and stochastic interventions that can restore positivity by changing the estimand; that is the estimand-class response the agenda already proposes, not a diagnostic that reports which histories lack support or what fraction of the target population is unsupported.


What does close most of the stated gap is recent prior art the agenda does not cite. Danelian et al. (Journal of Causal Inference 2023; 10.1515/jci-2022-0032) introduced PoRT, a regression-tree diagnostic that flags in-sample positivity violations as interpretable covariate-defined subgroups, with implementation in the CRAN package RISCA (port). Chatton et al. (Epidemiology 2025; 10.1097/EDE.0000000000001902) extend this to longitudinal static and dynamic strategies as sPoRT, explicitly motivated by the inadequacy of inspecting cumulative inverse-probability weights: weight products can flag sparsity under correctly specified propensity models but do not name the problematic subgroups. In their HIV ART reanalysis, sPoRT returns time-updated subgroups with size as a share of those who should follow the rule (e.g., a CD4/WAZ-defined cell of n*=43, 5.4% of those assigned to initiate at 6 months) and recommended responses include redesign of the rule, exclusion of structurally unsupported baseline strata as a design decision, and switch to alternative estimands. Ring and Schomaker (Journal of Causal Inference 2026; 10.1515/jci-2025-0007; arXiv:2502.11820) add a kernel-based, estimand-specific sparsity diagnostic for continuous treatments and MTPs that reports effective data points per intervened observation, supports comparing alternative estimands before estimation, and is tied to the CICI / lmtp ecosystem. Moodie and Schulz (Statistics in Medicine 2025; 10.1002/sim.70194) give a hat-value style diagnostic for continuous exposures. Together these tools deliver the three quantities the problem says weight histograms do not: unsupported fraction (via subgroup size or near-zero EDP mass), which histories fail (tree leaves or low-EDP units), and guidance on the estimand that remains identifiable (rule redesign, population restriction, or MTP choice).
What remains open, so a full “solved” vote would be wrong: (1) no agreed support threshold (α, β in PoRT/sPoRT; kernel bandwidth in Ring) is still a free estimand decision; (2) partial-identification bounds for the unsupported strata are not a packaged, routine output of these diagnostics; (3) the methods are not first-class diagnostics inside the main TTE stacks the agenda names (TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, lmtp, WeightIt/cobalt still center weight and balance summaries rather than history-level support maps); (4) very high-dimensional continuous longitudinal histories remain hard to plot as a single “causal support map,” which is a packaging and reporting problem more than an identification one. Searches that returned no stronger closer: TTE-package release notes / PRs for TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, gfoRmulaICE, lmtp, WeightIt, MatchIt, cobalt, CICI for a history-level support map; TARGET / HARPER / STaRT-RWE / ENCePP / FDA-RWE 2025–2026 guidance mandating unsupported-fraction reporting; arXiv/medRxiv 2024–2026 for partial-ID bounds specifically for positivity-unsupported TTE strata as standard practice. Bottom line: the claim that standard weight diagnostics hide the real object is still right for modal practice, but the claim that the field has no method that names unsupported histories is no longer true after PoRT (2023), sPoRT (2025), and Ring–Schomaker (2026). title: The visit process is treated as a nuisance to be imputed rather than as part of the causal structure
text:
Statement
Biomarkers and diagnoses are observed when a patient attends care and a clinician orders a test. That visit process depends on latent severity, on prior treatment and often on an impending outcome, so missing-at-random conditional on the recorded history can fail precisely because the recording is itself informative, last observation carried forward constructs a history in which the absence of measurement was itself evidence, and conditioning on having been observed can induce selection bias. Three estimator families now address this: multiply robust estimation under covariate-driven observation times, calibrated inverse probability weights under irregular visits, and continuous-time weights built from a marked point process. Inverse-intensity weighting handles conditionally independent visiting when the intensity model is correct and observation positivity holds; visiting that depends on a latent state needs further identifying assumptions or a sensitivity analysis. Applied emulations continue to use complete case or last observation carried forward, and enter healthcare use as a baseline confounder rather than as a process.

title: The visit process is treated as a nuisance to be imputed rather than as part of the causal structure
text:
Why it is open
The remaining methodological case is the one that matters most in practice: visiting driven by a latent severity the record does not contain, which no observation model can condition on. Weight instability is driven by small conditional observation probabilities and by intensity-model misspecification, and calibration of the intensity model does not validate it, so the diagnostic available does not settle whether the weights are trustworthy. The larger gap is adoption rather than method, and adoption is slow because modeling the visit process multiplies the nuisance components and therefore the positivity requirements, so the more faithful model can be the less identifiable one.

Work
What it contributes




Goldstein BA, Bhavsar NA, Phelan M, Pencina MJ. How and when informative visit processes can bias inference when using electronic health records data for clinical research. J Am Med Inform Assoc 2019

title: The visit process is treated as a nuisance to be imputed rather than as part of the causal structure
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Adopt the estimators that exist rather than defaulting to complete case or last observation carried forward, and state which assumption the chosen one requires: conditionally independent visiting, or a latent-state model with its own identifying conditions. Model visits as recurrent events or point processes jointly with treatment and outcome, and include healthcare use in the causal diagram as a process so conditioning decisions can be read off the graph. Report the dispersion of the observation weights and the conditional observation probabilities rather than the marginal visit rate, and pair a latent-state analysis with a sensitivity analysis, since calibration of an intensity model is not validation of it.

title: The visit process is treated as a nuisance to be imputed rather than as part of the causal structure
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source said. “Biomarkers and diagnoses are observed when a patient attends care and a clinician orders a test. That visit process depends on latent severity, on prior treatment and often on an impending outcome, so record-based covariate histories are irregular and selectively missing in a way that carries clinical information. Missing-at-random conditional on the recorded history can therefore fail precisely because the recording is itself informative. Standard handling, and last observation carried forward in particular, constructs an artificial history in which a patient’s state is asserted to be unchanged over an interval during which the absence of measurement was itself evidence about their state.”
What was wrong with it. Estimators that model the observation process jointly with treatment and outcome exist in three separate families, so the entry’s implication that the analyst has no principled option was wrong. Two further corrections: inverse-intensity weighting handles conditionally independent visiting when the intensity model is correct and observation positivity holds, and weight instability comes from small conditional observation probabilities and misspecification rather than from marginal visit-rate heterogeneity on its own.
Dissent. literature dissented (overstated): The entry says standard handling constructs artificial histories and that modeling visits jointly with treatment and outcome multiplies nuisance components without a worked solution. Three separate estimator families in the corpus contradict the strong reading. A 2024 Biometrics paper proposes a multiply robust estimator for marginal structural models under irregularly spaced, covariate-driven observation times and shows it is more flexible and more efficient than the previously proposed doubly weighted estimator. A 2023 BMC Medical Research Methodology paper gives calibrated inverse probability weights for marginal structural models under irregular visits with an unmeasured confounder. A 2025 Statistics in Medicine paper builds continuous-time weights from a marked point process for the same reason. What survives is an adoption claim rather than a methods claim: these estimators exist and applied emulation pipelines do not use them, and healthcare use is still entered as a baseline confounder rather than modeled as a process. grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): Inverted-prior search finds methods that put the visit process in the causal or estimating structure, so the problem is not open as a pure absence of methodology. It is not fully solved either: the report’s hard tradeoffs remain live, and the comparative evaluation it proposes has not been delivered for sustained-strategy target trial emulation under a known, treatment-dependent visiting mechanism.
Cited works first. Goldstein et al. (JAMIA 2019; 10.1093/jamia/ocz148) characterize when informative visits bias EHR association analyses; that paper diagnoses the mechanism and does not close it. Wang et al. (npj Digit Med 2026; 10.1038/s41746-026-02563-z) elevate the observation process to an operational constraint on whether an EHR can realize a target trial protocol element. Secondary commentary on that paper treats the contribution as specification-versus-realization discipline, not as a solved estimator. Both strengthen the claim that the issue is still on the agenda; neither resolves identification or estimation under treatment-dependent visiting.
Prior art that treats visits as structure rather than pure nuisance: (i) inverse-intensity-of-visit (IIW) theory and software for irregular longitudinal data (Pullenayegum line; CRAN IrregLong with Cox visit-intensity weights and IIW-GEE), still actively refined in 2025 on visit-model variable selection and selection of patients with no follow-up; (ii) parametric g-formula software that models a random measurement or visit process jointly with covariates for sustained strategies (gfoRmula’s visitprocess argument: visit indicators attached to intermittently measured confounders, with last-measured values and a cap on consecutive missed visits); (iii) Kalia et al. (BMC Med Res Methodol 2023; 10.1186/s12874-022-01831-2), calibrated inverse probability weights for marginal structural models under irregular visits, with Monte Carlo evaluation; (iv) Kalia et al. (Stat Med 2025; 10.1002/sim.70102), continuous-time MSM weights factored as visit intensity times dose (marked point process) on primary-care EHR for cumulative SGLT-2i exposure and recurrent UTI, explicitly motivated by informative visit timing. Coulombe et al. (Stat Methods Med Res 2023) combine inverse intensity of visit weights with individualized treatment rules in longitudinal observational data, which is related but not full sustained-strategy TTE.
What remains open, and why a full solved vote fails. IIW and continuous-time visit weights still require sequential positivity for the visit intensity and can be unstable when intensities vary sharply across patients; Kalia 2025 itself discusses extreme weights, stabilization, and constrained optimal weights, not elimination of the variance problem the report flags. Joint visit–treatment–outcome models still multiply nuisance components and positivity requirements; that structural cost is not removed by packaging. gfoRmula’s visit process assumes a discrete grid and a correctly specified visit model, and still encodes non-visit intervals via last measured values, so it does not by itself refute the LOCF critique for continuous-time EHR generation. No 2024–2026 paper or package release was found that runs the report’s proposed horse race (complete case, LOCF, MI, IIW, joint latent-state targeted learning) on data generated with a known treatment-dependent visiting mechanism in a sustained-strategy TTE design. Method proposals and single-setting applications therefore count as partial, not full, resolution.
Package and guidance scan. IrregLong and gfoRmula implement visit or measurement process handling; TrialEmulation, lmtp, ltmle, WeightIt, MatchIt, cobalt, ipw, adjustedCurves, riskRegression, zEpid, causallib, lifelines, and scikit-survival did not surface merged work that closes this gap for informative EHR visit processes under sustained strategies. 2025–2026 RWE guidances (FDA RWE, EMA/HMA registry, ICH E9(R1), TARGET, HARPER/STaRT-RWE, ENCePP, ISPE, NICE) frame data-generation and missingness issues at a high level; none was found that settles a preferred causal handling of informative visits for TTE.
Caveat on the claim as stated. Applied TTE and EHR pipelines still often grid time and carry forward or impute under MAR, so the nuisance framing is still a fair description of common practice. The methodological literature has long refused that framing, so a reader who only knows IIW, gfoRmula visitprocess, or continuous-time marked point process MSMs would find the absolute statement overstated. The agenda item that remains is comparative, practical, and identification-theoretic under realistic visit heterogeneity, not the invention of the first joint visit model.

title: Subgroup effects are estimated where overlap is worst, and the groups with worst overlap are often the protected ones
text: LRN-04 Partially addressed High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Subgroup effects are estimated where overlap is worst, and the groups with worst overlap are often the protected ones
text:
Statement
Causal forests and meta-learners estimate heterogeneous treatment effects and inherit every identification assumption of the base analysis without relaxing any of them. A subgroup analysis therefore requires subgroup-specific assessment of exchangeability, measurement validity, positivity and uncertainty, and apparent heterogeneity can reflect differential measurement or differential access rather than differential biology. Two further requirements are routinely skipped. Adaptively chosen subgroups need selection-aware inference, because the reported interval otherwise conditions on a subgroup the data chose. And restricting to regions with adequate overlap changes the target population rather than fixing the estimate, so it has to be reported as a change of question. Where the groups with the poorest support are the protected groups the analysis was undertaken to examine, that has to be demonstrated in the data at hand rather than assumed, and it is neither demonstrated nor required to be.

title: Subgroup effects are estimated where overlap is worst, and the groups with worst overlap are often the protected ones
text:
Why it is open
Overlap within a subgroup is a property of the data that no estimator improves, and restricting to where it holds removes the subgroups a fairness analysis exists to report on. Distinguishing effect modification from differential measurement requires validation data within each subgroup, which is scarcest where the subgroup is smallest. Honest sample splitting and selection-aware inference both cost precision in exactly the strata that are already imprecise, so the statistically correct analysis is the one least able to say anything.

title: Subgroup effects are estimated where overlap is worst, and the groups with worst overlap are often the protected ones
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Feuerriegel S, Frauen D, Melnychuk V, et al. Causal machine learning for predicting treatment outcomes. Nat Med 2024;30:958-968
States that causal machine learning supports individualized effect estimation only under the same identification assumptions as conventional methods, which is the constraint subgroup analyses routinely ignore.


Target trial emulation under nonmutually exclusive assignment. Am J Epidemiol 2026;195(4):1045
Shows overlap defeating advanced adjustment, which is the mechanism by which a subgroup estimate fails.

title: Subgroup effects are estimated where overlap is worst, and the groups with worst overlap are often the protected ones
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Report subgroup-specific data support, calibration and uncertainty next to every subgroup effect, so a wide and poorly supported estimate cannot be read as a finding, and show the support of protected groups in the data at hand rather than asserting it. Use honest sample splitting and selection-aware inference for adaptively chosen subgroups, and state overlap restriction as a change of target population when it is used. Evaluate not only whether benefit varies across groups but whether the emulation’s identification assumptions hold equally across them, since differential measurement and differential access are alternative explanations for the same pattern.

title: Subgroup effects are estimated where overlap is worst, and the groups with worst overlap are often the protected ones
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Causal forests and meta-learners estimate heterogeneous treatment effects, and they inherit every identification assumption of the base analysis without relaxing any of them. Subgroup discovery adds three specific hazards: confounding that varies by subgroup, multiplicity across the many subgroups a flexible learner implicitly examines, and limited overlap within small strata. Apparent heterogeneity can therefore reflect differential measurement, differential healthcare access or model extrapolation rather than differential biology. The distributional problem is that the groups with the least data and the poorest overlap are frequently the protected groups whose effects the analysis was undertaken to examine, so the least reliable estimates carry the most weight in interpretation.”
What was wrong with it. The claim that protected groups have the poorest overlap is an empirical claim about a particular dataset and has to be shown there rather than assumed. Adaptive subgroup selection also needs selection-aware inference specifically, and restricting to regions of adequate overlap changes the target population rather than repairing the estimate.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Subgroup estimation inside emulations is being done carefully in places the entry does not credit. A 2026 European Journal of Epidemiology paper extends a CONFIRM emulation to subgroups explicitly, a 2026 Alzheimer’s and Dementia paper estimates heterogeneous statin effects on dementia with causal machine learning inside an emulation, and a 2026 Epidemiology paper nests a target study within a target trial specifically to evaluate intervention effects on disparities, which is the equity question the entry raises. What remains is the reporting requirement: none of these establishes that subgroup-specific data support and calibration must be reported alongside every subgroup effect, and none tests whether the emulation’s assumptions differ across groups. Cites 10.1097/ede.0000000000002024: Provides a framework for the equity question the entry raises, within the emulation setting.. Cites 10.1007/s10654-026-01379-1: A worked subgroup extension of an emulation, showing the practice exists.. Cites 10.1002/alz.71178: Applies causal machine learning for heterogeneity inside an emulation, which is the combination the entry describes as hazardous..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Conditional and subgroup effects require the relevant consistency, conditional exchangeability, and positivity conditions within the target subgroups; flexible estimators do not create missing support. However, multiplicity is specifically a problem when adaptively discovered subgroups or contrasts are selected and interpreted inferentially, not an automatic defect of every conditional-effect estimator. Whether protected groups have the poorest overlap is an empirical, dataset-specific claim that must be demonstrated rather than presumed. Validation data are one way to distinguish effect modification from differential measurement, but the categorical requirement is too strong because additional measurement models or identifying assumptions may also be used. Honest estimation, shrinkage, and overlap restriction can improve inference, but shrinkage does not restore identification and restriction changes the target population. Causal-effect calibration is also not directly observable and must be defined through identifiable group-level contrasts or external validation. No package capability claim is present.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. Feuerriegel et al. (2024) again bind individualized causal ML to classical identification assumptions; that supports the problem’s premise without solving subgroup practice. Tools already recommended in the agenda exist in partial form: honest sample splitting in causal forests (Wager and Athey lineage), propensity trimming and common-support restriction, and various hierarchical or shrinkage approaches to unstable strata. Recent applied causal-forest work still documents poor within-stratum overlap and relies on post hoc trimming (e.g., 2025 Scientific Reports-style pipelines). What remains open is the joint operational problem the statement names: subgroup and protected-group HTE is often the scientific target; those strata systematically have the worst overlap and measurement quality; and there is no adopted standard that reports subgroup-specific data support, calibration, and differential assumption plausibility next to every CATE so that a poorly supported protected-group estimate cannot be read as a finding. Overlap is a data property no estimator repairs. Fairness-aware HTE and group-bias CATE work is active on arXiv and conference tracks but has not certified subgroup effects under differential access and measurement. Status remains open; the caveat is that honesty, trimming, and shrinkage are available components, not a field solution to protected-stratum extrapolation.

glm

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and correctly identifies that overlap is a property of the data that cannot be fixed by the estimator, and that this disproportionately affects protected groups. The reasons given for it being open logically support the claim. The scope and severity are proportionate to the real-world cost of misinterpreting subgroup effects.

Decision path

title: Automated protocol translation can change the estimand while producing valid code
text: LRN-02 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: Automated protocol translation can change the estimand while producing valid code
text:
Statement
Systems now translate trial descriptions into cohort definitions or analysis code, and natural language processing extracts eligibility information from unstructured notes. The failure mode is not that they crash. It is that validly executing code implements a different estimand: a mistranslated temporal condition, an ambiguous eligibility phrase resolved to the wrong operationalization, a join that reads treatment before eligibility as treatment after it. None of that is visible in the output, which is a working pipeline returning a plausible number, and downstream numerical plausibility does not validate the translation. Semantic fidelity is testable, against independently specified protocols, expert annotations, reference implementations and synthetic patients built so each temporal condition has a case that distinguishes the correct reading from the plausible wrong one. No such regime is required or routine, and the artifact under review remains the number rather than the specification.

title: Automated protocol translation can change the estimand while producing valid code
text:
Why it is open
Temporal logic is where these systems fail and where testing is hardest: the difference between treatment before eligibility assessment and treatment after it is one word in the specification and one join condition in the code, and both execute. A gold-standard cohort for a real dataset is often unavailable, which removes the most direct test and leaves the indirect ones, each of which costs the effort the automation was adopted to save. The systems are also spreading faster than any validation convention, now reaching concept-set authoring as well as protocol translation.

title: Automated protocol translation can change the estimand while producing valid code
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Kim, et al. From study design to executable code: automating target trial emulation with large language models. JAMIA Open 2026
Builds the translation from study design to executable emulation code, which is the system whose failure modes this problem concerns.


Wang, et al. An operational target trial emulation framework for causal inference using electronic health records. npj Digit Med 2026
Specifies the operational mapping from protocol component to record-level definition, which is the interface a compiler would have to respect.

title: Automated protocol translation can change the estimand while producing valid code
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Treat automation as a constrained compiler: a human-authored causal specification, a typed intermediate representation, and data-source-specific code generated from it, with temporal-logic validation applied to the intermediate representation rather than to the output. Require unit tests over synthetic patients constructed so that each temporal condition has a case distinguishing the correct reading from the plausible wrong one, and test semantic fidelity against independently specified protocols and reference implementations where they exist. Require dual human sign-off on the specification and the generated cohort counts, and publish both, so what is reviewed is the specification and not the estimate.

title: Automated protocol translation can change the estimand while producing valid code
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Systems now translate trial descriptions into cohort definitions or analysis code, and natural language processing extracts eligibility information from unstructured notes. The failure mode of these systems is not that they crash. It is that they silently substitute a different estimand: mistranslating a temporal condition, resolving an ambiguous eligibility phrase to the wrong operationalization, or emitting code that is syntactically valid and causally invalid. None of these failures is visible in the output, which is a working pipeline returning a plausible number. What is missing is a validation regime that treats generated code as an untrusted artifact rather than as a productivity gain.”
What was wrong with it. The entry argued that validation is impossible because the correct cohort is what the pipeline was built to produce. That is too strong: semantic fidelity can be tested against independently specified protocols, expert annotations, reference implementations and synthetic temporal boundary cases even when a gold-standard cohort for the real dataset is unavailable.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): Automated translation from study design to executable emulation code exists, and agentic authoring of OMOP concept sets from natural language is now being attempted, so the systems the entry describes are real and multiplying. Nothing in the corpus supplies the validation regime the entry asks for: no typed intermediate representation, no temporal-logic validation, no synthetic test patients constructed to distinguish the correct reading of a temporal condition from the plausible wrong one, and no dual sign-off requirement. The gap between capability and validation is the claim, and the corpus shows only the capability half.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. Automated translation from study design to executable emulation code exists, and agentic authoring of OMOP concept sets from natural language is now being attempted, so the systems the entry describes are real and multiplying. Nothing in the corpus supplies the validation regime the entry asks for: no typed intermediate representation, no temporal-logic validation, no synthetic test patients constructed to distinguish the correct reading of a temporal condition from the plausible wrong one, and no dual sign-off requirement. The gap between capability and validation is the claim, and the corpus shows only the capability half. Cites 10.1093/jamiaopen/ooag131: Builds the translation the entry is concerned about, which establishes the capability without supplying the validation.. Cites 10.64898/2026.06.02.26354704: Extends automation to phenotype definition, which is the component where a silent error changes the cohort..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Executable code can silently change eligibility, time zero, assignment, follow-up, or the resulting estimand, so the core risk is real. However, it is false that such errors are necessarily invisible or that no reference answer can exist. Independently authored specifications, expert-labeled records, hand-coded reference implementations, differential testing, and synthetic boundary-case patients can provide component-level or end-to-end reference answers. The report’s own proposed synthetic-patient tests contradict the categorical no-reference-answer claim. Agreement of a downstream effect estimate is insufficient evidence of semantic correctness, but evaluating against an external randomized benchmark is not literally circular. Typed intermediate representations and temporal tests reduce risk without proving semantic equivalence for every real-world mapping. No package capability claim is present.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Kim et al. (JAMIA Open 2026; THESEUS) and Wang et al. (npj Digit Med 2026) build or specify automated protocol-to-code and operational EHR mappings; they are the systems whose silent estimand-shift risk the problem names, not fixes of that risk. Lee et al. (JMIR Med Inform 2025) validate LLM-generated trial-criteria queries for functional correctness, which is partial operational testing but not temporal-logic unit tests that distinguish treatment-before versus treatment-after eligibility. Girshovitz, Zeltzer, and Gilad-Bachrach (arXiv:2607.21173, 2026) propose ARA: structured protocol intermediate form, SCM synthetic failure scenarios, and adversarial validation so that silent success is replaced by visible protocol or diagnostic failure. That is closely aligned with the report direction, yet it is a proposal with a small econometric-style benchmark; it does not establish a standard validation regime for TTE automation, dual human sign-off on specification and cohort counts, or synthetic patients that isolate each temporal join. Guidance (TARGET 2025 reporting; FDA/EMA RWE documents) addresses transparency of human-designed emulations, not untrusted machine-generated code. No CRAN or GitHub merge was found that ships a constrained TTE compiler with temporal unit tests. Silent estimand substitution under syntactically valid pipelines remains open.

glm

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and correctly identifies the silent estimand substitution as a structural risk in automated translation. The reasons given for it being open (lack of reference answers, circularity of downstream evaluation) strongly support the claim. The scope is appropriate and the severity is proportionate to the cost of a wrong estimand.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
text: GMT-04 Confirmed open High priority Established Tractability 5/5

title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
text:
Statement
The available estimators differ in what they assume rather than only in how they perform. Active-comparator new-user designs with regression or propensity adjustment handle baseline initiation and not treatment-confounder feedback. Matching gives a transparent population, discards information, and often leaves its estimand unstated. Marginal structural models represent regime effects directly and are unstable under extreme weights. The parametric g-formula supports flexible estimands and is sensitive to sequential outcome-model misspecification. G-estimation avoids modeling the treatment-free outcome distribution and is technically demanding. Longitudinal targeted learning is doubly robust, computationally heavy and sensitive to practical positivity. No estimator is defensible as a universal default, and a study reporting one reports a number whose dependence on that choice is unknown: nothing requires the choice to be justified against the estimand and the data structure, and nothing requires a prespecified alternative targeting the same contrast.

title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
text:
Why it is open
Comparing estimators multiplies the analysis cost and can produce disagreement the paper then has to explain, which is a strong disincentive. There is no accepted way to report disagreement between estimators targeting one estimand under different nuisance assumptions: it is neither a sensitivity analysis in the usual sense nor a robustness check. Simulation evidence comparing the families is fragmented across papers with different generating mechanisms, so no synthesis exists that would justify a default even if one were wanted.

title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Robins JM, Hernán MA, Brumback B. Marginal structural models and causal inference in epidemiology. Epidemiology 2000;11(5):550-560
The reference for weighted estimation of regime effects, one of the three families a comparison would have to include.


ltmle: Longitudinal Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation. CRAN
Implements longitudinal TMLE, IPTW and g-computation in one place, which makes the three-family comparison feasible in a single analysis.


lmtp: Non-Parametric Causal Effects of Feasible Interventions Based on Modified Treatment Policies. CRAN
Implements targeted and sequentially doubly robust estimators for point and longitudinal modified treatment policies.


Su L, et al. TrialEmulation: an R package to emulate target trials for causal analysis of observational time-to-event data. arXiv 2024
Provides the sequence-of-trials implementation with intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses.

title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Require that the prespecified estimator be justified against the exact estimand, data structure, overlap and nuisance assumptions, and that at least one prespecified alternative targeting the same contrast be reported where feasible, so estimation sensitivity is visible without mandating three families in every study. Build a public benchmark with realistic observation processes and missingness on which the families are compared under a common generating mechanism, turning the fragmented simulation evidence into a synthesis. Score methods on failure awareness as well as bias and coverage: an estimator returning a narrow interval in a deliberately non-identifiable scenario has failed the test that matters most.

title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “The available estimators differ in what they assume rather than only in how they perform. Active-comparator new-user designs with regression or propensity adjustment handle baseline initiation and not treatment-confounder feedback. Matching gives a transparent population and discards information, with an estimand that is often left unstated. Marginal structural models represent regime effects directly and are unstable under extreme weights. The parametric g-formula supports flexible estimands and is sensitive to sequential outcome-model misspecification. G-estimation avoids modeling the treatment-free outcome distribution and is technically demanding. Longitudinal targeted learning is doubly robust and computationally heavy and sensitive to practical positivity. A study reporting one of these reports a number whose dependence on that choice is unknown, and nothing requires that at least one weighting, one outcome-modeling and one doubly robust estimator be compared on the same data.”
What was wrong with it. The proposed requirement was too strong. Every emulation need not compare all three estimator families; what a study owes is a justification of its prespecified estimator against the exact estimand, data structure, overlap and nuisance assumptions, with prespecified alternatives targeting the same contrast where that is feasible.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The claim that no estimator is defensible as a default is well supported by the fragmentation the corpus shows, and the proposed remedy is partly in progress. Benchmarking of data-adaptive against investigator-specified confounding adjustment exists, and a 2026 evaluation compares statistical and deep learning methods for bias in a heart failure emulation. Neither supplies the public benchmark under a common generating mechanism that the entry asks for, and neither establishes a requirement that each study compare a weighting, an outcome-modelling and a doubly robust estimator. The overstatement is small: the entry’s implication that no comparative evidence exists is wrong, while its claim that no synthesis or requirement exists holds. Cites 10.1093/jamia/ocaf204: Benchmarks adjustment strategies against one another, which is the comparison the entry says is not done.. Cites 10.1038/s41467-026-74999-6: Compares statistical against deep learning estimation for bias within a single emulation, spanning two of the three families..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

not-a-problem / overstated. The absence of a universally preferred estimator is expected because estimator choice must follow the estimand, intervention, longitudinal structure, overlap and plausible nuisance assumptions. It is not itself a methodological defect, and a mandatory three-family comparison is neither necessary nor sufficient for validity. Alternative estimators are informative only when they genuinely target the same intervention, population, censoring handling and effect measure. Their disagreement is reasonably described as sensitivity to estimation assumptions, although it does not identify which estimate is correct; agreement can reflect shared identification failure. Several method summaries are too broad. Baseline active-comparator adjustment is inadequate for sustained per-protocol strategies with treatment-confounder feedback, but can be appropriate for a treatment-policy effect of initiation. Matching need not always discard observations, and its estimand depends on the matching design. The parametric g-formula models the longitudinal covariate and outcome law, not merely an outcome regression. Double robustness belongs to specified targeted estimators under stated nuisance conditions, not longitudinal targeted learning without qualification. TrialEmulation 0.0.4.11 is source-supported: its NAMESPACE exports trial_sequence and expand_trials, and its DESCRIPTION states that it estimates intention-to-treat and per-protocol effects. I abstain on the cited ltmle and lmtp capabilities because neither package is vendored under documentation/refs/packages/.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. No estimator family is established as a default for longitudinal target-trial emulation of sustained strategies, and no current reporting or protocol standard requires a three-family comparison (weighting, outcome modeling, doubly robust) on the same data. Prior art that does not close the gap: (i) simulation comparisons of g-computation, IPTW/OW, and TMLE exist but are fragmented across data-generating mechanisms and often point-treatment or externally controlled trial settings (for example Schuler and Rose; Ren et al. 2023); (ii) software already makes multi-family analysis feasible (ltmle implements LTMLE, IPTW, and g-computation; lmtp implements sequential DR and related estimators; TrialEmulation covers sequence-of-trials ITT/PP), which lowers cost but does not create a requirement or a shared benchmark; (iii) TARGET 2025 (JAMA/BMJ) is a reporting guideline for target-trial emulations and does not mandate multi-estimator families; HARPER and STaRT-RWE structure protocols and sensitivity analyses without requiring weighting-plus-outcome-plus-DR comparison under a common estimand. No public continuous-time or informative-visit benchmark synthesizing the fragmented simulations was found. The problem’s claim about incentives against multi-estimator reporting remains accurate. Searches: comparing IPTW g-formula TMLE longitudinal target trial multi-method 2024 2025; TARGET checklist multiple estimators; HARPER STaRT-RWE sensitivity g-methods; Schuler Rose TMLE IPW g-computation.

glm

open / supported-with-caveat. The claim is largely coherent and the reason given for openness (cost of comparison, no accepted reporting framework for disagreement, fragmented simulation evidence) genuinely supports it. However, the headline assertion ‘no estimator is defensible as a default’ is stronger than the body of the statement warrants. The body argues that estimators differ in assumptions and that no synthesis exists to justify a universal default, which is defensible. But ‘no estimator is defensible as a default’ could be read as claiming that in no specific setting is any estimator a reasonable default, which would be overstated—there are settings where, given known structure, one family is clearly preferred. The intended reading is that no single estimator is defensible as a universal default across the heterogeneous landscape of longitudinal causal problems, and on that reading the claim holds. The severity is proportionate: the cost of a wrong default estimator choice is a biased or unstable causal estimate presented without context.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex
