title: Transporting an observational estimate compounds sampling assumptions on top of confounding assumptions with no accounting
text: EST-02 Partially addressed High priority Promising Tractability 3/5

title: Transporting an observational estimate compounds sampling assumptions on top of confounding assumptions with no accounting
text:
Statement
An internally valid estimate need not apply to the health system, population or calendar period where the decision will be made. Transporting an observational contrast requires treatment exchangeability in the source, effect exchangeability across samples conditional on a sufficient measured set, and positivity for both treatment and sampling. A sufficient set is weaker than every effect modifier: modifiers that do not differ across populations or that are irrelevant after conditioning need not be observed. Transport estimators are now being applied to emulations, including post hoc standardization of emulations to their trial populations inside a benchmarking program. What remains is the accounting. If either exchangeability condition fails, source outcomes and target covariates alone cannot generally identify the resulting bias or apportion it between the two conditions, and no reporting practice attempts either.

title: Transporting an observational estimate compounds sampling assumptions on top of confounding assumptions with no accounting
text:
Why it is open
Both assumption sets are untestable and they fail in correlated ways: a health system whose case mix differs is usually also one whose confounding structure and treatment availability differ, so a single sensitivity parameter cannot represent the joint failure and separate parameters are not separately identified. Unmeasured effect modification is undetectable in the source population by construction. Combining transport with flexible representation learning risks erasing the effect modification transport is meant to preserve, because predictive invariance and causal invariance are different properties.

title: Transporting an observational estimate compounds sampling assumptions on top of confounding assumptions with no accounting
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Westreich D, Edwards JK, Lesko CR, Stuart E, Cole SR. Transportability of trial results using inverse odds of sampling weights. Am J Epidemiol 2017;186(8):1010-1014
Gives the inverse-odds-of-sampling weighting estimator for transporting a trial result to a target population.


Manke-Reimers M, et al. When, why and how are estimated effects transported between populations? A scoping review. Eur J Epidemiol 2025
Maps what applied transport studies actually do, which is where the finding that flexible estimators are underused comes from.

title: Transporting an observational estimate compounds sampling assumptions on top of confounding assumptions with no accounting
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Develop causal representation learning for transportability that balances populations only on representations sufficient for effect modification rather than on everything predictive, combined with targeted standardization and site-level random effects. Derive bounds under unmeasured effect modification and report them with the point estimate, so a transported number carries its own fragility rather than inheriting the source’s precision. Simulate populations that differ in covariates, treatment mechanisms, baseline hazards and effect modifiers separately, so each source of non-transportability is measurable rather than confounded with the others.

title: Transporting an observational estimate compounds sampling assumptions on top of confounding assumptions with no accounting
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “An internally valid estimate need not apply to the health system, population or calendar period where the decision will be made. Weighting, outcome modeling and doubly robust transport estimators all exist, and all of them require that the effect modifiers be measured, that the populations overlap, and that effects be conditionally exchangeable across samples. Applied transport work still mostly uses conventional sampling weights or outcome models despite the more flexible alternatives. The deeper issue is that transporting an observational estimate stacks the sampling-exchangeability assumption on top of the treatment-exchangeability assumption, and no current reporting practice shows how the two compound or which one a given discrepancy should be charged to.”
What was wrong with it. Identification does not require that every effect modifier be measured; it requires a sufficient set. Modifiers that do not differ across populations, or that are irrelevant after conditioning, need not be observed. Transport estimators are also reaching emulation practice faster than the entry allowed, including inside benchmarking programs.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Transport methods are reaching emulation practice faster than the entry allows. A 2026 Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics paper performs post hoc population standardization of trial emulation studies in claims data within RCT-DUPLICATE, which is transport applied to the benchmarking corpus itself. Nurse home visiting was emulated in the policy-relevant population using targeted learning and transport, and the scoping review the entry cites documents the practice broadly. What survives is the compounding claim: no reporting practice shows how sampling exchangeability and treatment exchangeability compound, or which of the two a discrepancy should be charged to. Cites 10.1002/cpt.70241: Standardizes emulations to trial populations inside the largest benchmarking program, which is transport applied where the entry says it is underused.. Cites 10.1093/ije/dyac092: Combines the target trial framework with transport and targeted learning to reach a policy-relevant population..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Transporting an observational effect does require distinct treatment-exchangeability and cross-sample exchangeability conditions, together with treatment and sampling positivity. The report overstates what must be measured: identification needs a sufficient transport set, not literally every effect modifier. Effect modifiers that do not differ across samples or are irrelevant after conditioning need not all be observed. A scalar sensitivity parameter can represent an aggregate joint bias, although it cannot uniquely decompose that bias without additional restrictions. The inability to charge a discrepancy to one assumption is chiefly nonidentification, not merely absent reporting. Representation learning or site random effects do not restore identification by themselves. The empirical claim about current practice is outside this technical vote.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Transport estimators (IOSW, outcome modeling, doubly robust/TMLE, calibration) are mature for trials and increasingly documented for observational sources; that is already acknowledged by the report’s Westreich citation and does not close the problem. The open core is accounting: transporting an observational estimate stacks treatment-exchangeability on sampling-exchangeability, both largely untestable, and no standard reporting practice decomposes a discrepancy between those failure modes. Scelo et al. (Front Epidemiol 2024; 10.3389/fepid.2024.1335241) explicitly lists the internal-validity and external-validity assumption blocks side by side, notes that most are untestable, and demonstrates TMLE transport from an observational birth cohort to a registry target; that formalizes the stack and does not provide joint sensitivity or attribution. Manke-Reimers et al. (Eur J Epidemiol 2025; 10.1007/s10654-025-01217-w), already cited, maps applied transport studies and underuse of flexible estimators; a scoping review of practice is evidence the gap remains, not a solution. Adamson et al. (Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf 2026; 10.1002/pds.70396) offers a stepwise transportability framework for comparative effectiveness and urges sensitivity for unmeasured effect modifiers, e-values, and tipping-point analyses; that is guidance and one-parameter sensitivity, not a joint compounding account that charges residual bias to confounding versus selection/effect-modification structure. Separate sensitivity tools for unmeasured confounding and for unmeasured selection/effect modification exist; they do not identify effects when both fail in correlated ways, and the discipline rule forbids treating sensitivity as solving identification. Causal representation learning for transport that preserves effect modification (rather than predictive invariance) remains workshop/early-methods work; no 2024–2026 applied TTE package (lmtp, ltmle, WeightIt, TrialEmulation, zEpid) was found that ships joint internal-plus-external fragility bounds with attribution. Queries run: transportability observational compounding/joint sensitivity; unmeasured effect modification bounds transport; Manke-Reimers and Adamson follow-ups; Scelo 2024 full text; CRL transport effect modifiers; CRAN/GitHub keyword checks for transport modules. Vote open: methods and guidance expanded; the compounding-accounting and attribution problem as stated is not solved.

glm

open / supported. The claim is coherent and pitched at the right level of generality. It accurately describes the compounding of sampling-exchangeability and treatment-exchangeability assumptions in transportability, and notes the lack of reporting practices to disentangle them. The reasons given for it being open (correlated failures of untestable assumptions, undetectable unmeasured effect modification, and the tension between predictive and causal invariance in representation learning) are valid and support the claim being open.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1/4) → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
text: GMT-01 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
text:
Statement
Identifying a sustained-strategy effect requires consistency, sequential exchangeability and positivity, and the estimator families differ in which nuisance components they need. When those components are fitted by machine learning, the model that predicts treatment best is not the model that minimizes the finite-sample error of the causal estimator: a highly adaptive learner can achieve excellent discrimination while returning near-zero treatment probabilities, poor longitudinal balance and invalid inference. Balance-calibrated weight fitting exists and has been applied, so the field is not selecting on prediction alone. What is missing is a criterion that combines predictive risk with the estimator-specific diagnostics that matter, longitudinal balance, weight tails and the remainder-rate condition, in one selection rule, and a default library tuned that way rather than for prediction.

title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
text:
Why it is open
The causal loss is not computable the way a predictive loss is, because the contrast being targeted is never observed, so the quantity one would cross-validate against does not exist as a label. Balance and weight-dispersion criteria are computable and are not losses in the decision-theoretic sense, and a learner can optimize them while fitting poorly. Which diagnostics apply depends on the estimator, so a single universal criterion is the wrong object and a family of estimator-specific ones has to be built and validated separately.

title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Robins JM, Hernán MA, Brumback B. Marginal structural models and causal inference in epidemiology. Epidemiology 2000;11(5):550-560
Introduces marginal structural models and inverse probability weighting for time-varying confounding affected by prior treatment. The nuisance models are parametric and their selection is not addressed.


Feuerriegel S, Frauen D, Melnychuk V, et al. Causal machine learning for predicting treatment outcomes. Nat Med 2024;30:958-968
Sets out what causal machine learning can and cannot do, and states that individualized effect estimation rests on the same identification assumptions as conventional methods.


ltmle: Longitudinal Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation. CRAN
Implements longitudinal TMLE, IPTW and g-computation, and accepts a SuperLearner library whose selection is left to the analyst.

title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Construct selection rules that combine predictive risk with longitudinal standardized differences, weight-tail behavior and an estimate of the influence-function remainder, specified per estimator rather than universally, and test whether they select models with lower causal bias than predictive cross-validation on the same data. Compare weighted marginal structural models, sequentially doubly robust estimators, longitudinal targeted learning and Bayesian g-computation under deliberate misspecification of each nuisance component in turn. Cross-fit at the patient level rather than the record level, and report the empirical standard-error ratio and convergence failures with the bias, since an estimator that fails to converge on a fifth of replicates is not competitive at any bias.

title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
The source said. “Marginal structural models, the parametric g-formula, g-estimation and longitudinal targeted learning all identify sustained-regime effects under sequential exchangeability and positivity, and all of them require nuisance models for treatment, censoring and outcome. When those nuisance models are fitted by machine learning, the model that predicts treatment best is not the model that produces the best causal estimate: a highly adaptive learner can achieve excellent discrimination while returning near-zero treatment probabilities, poor longitudinal balance and invalid inference. Standard cross-validation selects on prediction loss and is blind to all three. No selection criterion in routine use combines treatment prediction with longitudinal balance, weight dispersion and an estimate of the influence-function remainder, and no default library is tuned for the causal objective rather than the predictive one.”
What was wrong with it. Balance-based criteria for the weight model are already in use: calibrated weights fitted with SuperLearner have been implemented and applied to longitudinal cohorts, so the claim that no selection criterion departs from prediction was too strong. The identification requirements also include consistency alongside sequential exchangeability and positivity, and different estimators require different nuisance components, which the entry flattened.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The general claim, that predictive cross-validation is the wrong criterion for a nuisance model whose purpose is causal, is correct and is not new. What the entry misses is that criteria other than prediction are already in use for the weight model specifically. Calibrated weights fitted with SuperLearner have been implemented and applied to longitudinal diabetes cohorts, and calibration is precisely a balance criterion rather than a prediction criterion. Super learner for weight estimation under unknown weight-model specification was studied for marginal structural models as early as 2017. So the entry’s claim that no selection criterion in routine use combines prediction with balance overstates: balance-based weight fitting exists and is published. The part that survives is the combination the entry actually asks for, a single loss spanning prediction, longitudinal balance, weight dispersion and an influence-function remainder, and the absence of a default library tuned that way. Cites 10.1109/jbhi.2022.3175862: Fits marginal structural model weights with SuperLearner under a calibration criterion rather than a prediction criterion, in a longitudinal EHR setting with dynamic regimes.. Cites 10.1002/sim.7266: Studies super learner for the weight model specifically, which is the nuisance component the entry says selection is blind for.. Cites 10.1002/sim.9568: Treats cross-validation for dynamic treatment regimes directly, in the presence of competing risks..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The estimator-selection question is coherent, but the methodological setup is incorrect. Identification follows from the observed-data law plus consistency, sequential exchangeability, positivity and a well-defined intervention; estimators do not themselves identify effects. The methods listed do not all require treatment, censoring and outcome nuisance models. An IP-weighted MSM generally models treatment and censoring mechanisms; the parametric g-formula models the conditional evolution of covariates and outcomes without requiring a treatment model; standard g-estimation combines a structural model with a treatment model; longitudinal TMLE uses sequential outcome regressions and treatment or censoring mechanisms. Prediction-optimal tuning need not minimize causal error, but near-zero probabilities can reflect the true treatment process and practical positivity rather than excessive adaptivity. Predictive cross-validation does not optimize balance or weight dispersion, although those quantities are functions of its predictions and can be assessed separately. An influence-function remainder is not generally observable because it depends on unknown nuisance errors. The assertion that no routine criterion exists is a literature-coverage claim outside this audit. The ltmle capability claim is unverified because calibration.json pins only TrialEmulation and no ltmle source is vendored under documentation/refs/packages/.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Inverted-prior search did not find a routine selection criterion that jointly optimizes treatment prediction, longitudinal balance, weight dispersion, and an influence-function remainder for longitudinal nuisance models. SuperLearner (as used by ltmle and related stacks) still cross-validates predictive risk; CV-TMLE and related work improve targeting of the final parameter after nuisance fitting but do not replace predictive CV for the treatment, censoring, and outcome libraries themselves. Collaborative TMLE (C-TMLE) is the closest prior art: it selects confounder models using a targeted, collaborative criterion rather than pure prediction, and longitudinal/scalable C-TMLE variants exist. That is covariate-and-collaborative selection for TMLE, not a multi-metric SuperLearner loss for sustained-regime MSM, g-formula, g-estimation, or LTMLE libraries. Point-treatment work on balance-versus-discrimination for propensity scores (for example Diaz on balancing criteria) does not cover sequential longitudinal nuisance selection. Package surfaces checked in search (ltmle SuperLearner interface, SuperLearner defaults, SAS SUPERLEARNER 2024/2025) still select on predictive CV. No 2024 to 2026 AJE/Epidemiology/SiM-style paper or CRAN default library was found that implements the combined causal objective the problem names. Searches included: causal cross-validation SuperLearner longitudinal TMLE balance weight dispersion; causal loss OR targeted cross-validation nuisance MSM; collaborative TMLE longitudinal SuperLearner; propensity SuperLearner balance loss 2023 to 2026.

glm

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and well-scoped. It asserts that no selection criterion in routine use combines treatment prediction with longitudinal balance, weight dispersion, and an influence-function remainder—this is a claim about current practice, not about impossibility. The reason given for openness is structural: the causal loss (counterfactual contrast) is never observed, so there is no label to cross-validate against, and computable surrogates like balance are not proper decision-theoretic losses. This genuinely supports the problem being open. The one sentence about no default library being tuned for the causal objective touches on software, but the core claim is methodological. The severity is proportionate: a wrong default selection criterion would propagate bias into every downstream causal estimate.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1/4) → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
text:

title: Large databases yield small effective samples after eligibility, comparator restriction and weighting
text: GMT-03 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Large databases yield small effective samples after eligibility, comparator restriction and weighting
text:
Statement
A database of millions can carry very little information about a specific target trial once strict eligibility, active-comparator restriction and weighting have been applied, and extreme weights reduce the effective sample size far below the nominal count. Conventional asymptotic inference then becomes unreliable, most sharply for rare competing events and for subgroup effects, which are the quantities decision makers ask about. Papers continue to report the nominal number of patients, which for a weighted longitudinal analysis is not the quantity that governs the variance, and no convention requires the effective size to appear beside it.

title: Large databases yield small effective samples after eligibility, comparator restriction and weighting
text:
Why it is open
The effective sample size is estimator-specific and time-varying in a longitudinal analysis, so there is no single number to report and no convention for which to choose. Small-sample corrections in this setting have to account for the estimated weights as well as the outcome model, and that theory is thin. There is also no incentive to report a number that shrinks a study’s apparent size by an order of magnitude.

title: Large databases yield small effective samples after eligibility, comparator restriction and weighting
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Robins JM, Hernán MA, Brumback B. Marginal structural models and causal inference in epidemiology. Epidemiology 2000;11(5):550-560
Introduces the weighted estimator whose variance is governed by the weight distribution rather than by the record count.


Impact of near-positivity violations on IPTW-estimated marginal structural survival models with time-dependent covariates. Biom J 2025
Quantifies how near-positivity degrades weighted longitudinal survival estimation, which is the mechanism by which effective sample size collapses.


lmtp: Non-Parametric Causal Effects of Feasible Interventions Based on Modified Treatment Policies. CRAN
Targets shifted rather than deterministic interventions, one route to keeping the effective sample size usable.

title: Large databases yield small effective samples after eligibility, comparator restriction and weighting
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Investigate Bayesian hierarchical g-computation, targeted shrinkage, exact or permutation-based inference, outcome-adaptive case-control sampling and cross-site borrowing for the regime where the effective sample is small. Require that the effective sample size be reported alongside the nominal one at each follow-up time, so a reader sees the information actually available. Establish by simulation the point at which asymptotic intervals stop covering, as a function of the weight tail and the event rate, so the reporting threshold is empirical rather than conventional.

title: Large databases yield small effective samples after eligibility, comparator restriction and weighting
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “A database of millions can carry very little information about a specific target trial once strict eligibility, active-comparator restriction and weighting have been applied, and extreme weights reduce the effective sample size much further than the nominal count suggests. Conventional asymptotic inference then becomes unreliable, most sharply for rare competing events and for subgroup effects, which are precisely the quantities decision-makers ask about. Papers continue to report the nominal number of patients, which for a weighted longitudinal analysis is not the quantity that governs the variance.”
What was wrong with it. No auditor found the claim overstated. The statement is retained with the effect of near-positivity on weighted longitudinal survival estimation cited, which supplies the mechanism the entry asserts.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): Nothing in the corpus reports the effective sample size alongside the nominal one as a convention, nor establishes the point at which asymptotic intervals stop covering as a function of weight tail and event rate. Work on near-positivity violations in IPTW-estimated marginal structural survival models measures the consequence, which is the closest existing treatment, and it characterizes bias rather than supplying a reporting rule. The claim is a reporting and small-sample-inference gap rather than a missing estimator, which makes it harder to refute by finding a method paper and easier to confirm by observing practice.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. Nothing in the corpus reports the effective sample size alongside the nominal one as a convention, nor establishes the point at which asymptotic intervals stop covering as a function of weight tail and event rate. Work on near-positivity violations in IPTW-estimated marginal structural survival models measures the consequence, which is the closest existing treatment, and it characterizes bias rather than supplying a reporting rule. The claim is a reporting and small-sample-inference gap rather than a missing estimator, which makes it harder to refute by finding a method paper and easier to confirm by observing practice. Cites 10.1002/bimj.70093: Quantifies the consequence of near-positivity for weighted survival estimation, which is the mechanism by which effective sample size collapses..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The central claim is correct. Eligibility and comparator restrictions reduce the number of relevant independent patients, while concentrated positive weights reduce the Kish effective sample size through (sum w)^2 divided by sum(w^2). Rare events and subgroup restrictions can leave little information despite a large source database. The important caveat is that a weight-only effective sample size is not the information governing every estimator. In longitudinal emulations it is time-specific and must account for risk sets, events, repeated or cloned records, within-patient dependence, estimated nuisance functions and the outcome variance. A small calculated effective sample size therefore does not automatically invalidate asymptotic inference; validity also depends on independent-cluster counts, event counts, weight-tail moments and nuisance-estimation behavior. Reporting time-specific weight concentration is useful but cannot replace at-risk counts, event counts, overlap plots and influence-function or cluster-level variance diagnostics. Exact or permutation inference is not generally available in observational data without a known assignment mechanism. Shrinkage and cross-site borrowing add assumptions and cannot repair structural positivity failure or absent outcome information. Simulation can characterize a specified design but cannot produce a universal coverage threshold. The lmtp software claim is unverified because no pinned lmtp source is vendored.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The core claim survives: after eligibility, active-comparator restriction, and inverse-probability weighting, information can collapse far below the nominal N, and papers still lead with headcount rather than information. What exists does not close the agenda item. Kish-style ESS, WeightIt::ESS, and cobalt balance tables already report weight-based effective sample size (including longitudinal MSM balance displays); Zhang, Bujkiewicz, and Jackson (BMC Medical Research Methodology 2024; 10.1186/s12874-024-02412-1) add three ESS estimators aimed at population-adjusted indirect comparison and general weighted analyses. Those are diagnostics for precision loss, not small-sample inference for estimated longitudinal weights plus outcome models, not time-varying ESS conventions for MSM/LTMLE follow-up, and not a simulation standard for when asymptotic intervals stop covering as a function of weight tails and event rates. lmtp’s modified treatment policies help keep positivity usable but do not solve ESS reporting or finite-sample theory. No 2024 to 2026 reporting guideline (TARGET 2025, HARPER, STaRT-RWE, ENCePP) was found that requires ESS alongside nominal N at each follow-up time. Searches: effective sample size inverse probability weights MSM longitudinal 2024 2025; Zhang Bujkiewicz Jackson ESS; WeightIt ESS cobalt; small sample inference IPW MSM sandwich correction; TARGET ESS reporting. Vote open because the agenda’s open parts (estimator-specific time-varying ESS convention, weight-aware small-sample theory, reporting incentive) remain; partial software and population-adjustment ESS papers are caveats, not solutions.

glm

open / supported. The claim is well-constructed and proportionate. It describes a real statistical phenomenon (effective sample size collapse under weighting and restriction) and a real reporting gap (papers report nominal counts). The reason given for openness is practical and theoretical: effective sample size is estimator-specific and time-varying so there is no single number, small-sample correction theory for estimated weights is thin, and there is no incentive to report a smaller number. None of these are impossibility claims; they are claims about the absence of convention and theory. The scope is right—it does not claim all large databases are uninformative, only that they can be, and that the reporting does not reflect the information actually available.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R11:caveated(n=2)

title: Flexible estimation is presented as a remedy for identification failure
text: LRN-01 Confirmed open High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Flexible estimation is presented as a remedy for identification failure
text:
Statement
Identification is a property of the observed data together with the assumptions, not of the estimator. A flexible learner reduces approximation error in a nuisance function and cannot repair nonidentification, and the same smoothness that reduces that error extends the fit confidently into regions holding no observations. Support and overlap diagnostics can flag particular forms of extrapolation, and they depend on how support is defined and on the model producing them, so a passing diagnostic certifies nothing about sequential exchangeability, positivity or identification. The gap widens with high-dimensional treatment histories, where the region a prediction is being asked about is itself hard to characterize, and applied work continues to offer a more flexible learner as the response to a confounding or positivity concern.

title: Flexible estimation is presented as a remedy for identification failure
text:
Why it is open
Extrapolation is invisible in any conventional fit statistic: a model can have excellent cross-validated loss on the observed region and be entirely unconstrained off it. The regions that matter are conditional on a growing treatment and covariate history, so whether a given prediction is supported is itself a high-dimensional question, and any diagnostic answering it has to define support in a way that is a modeling choice rather than a fact. The professional incentive also points one way, since the flexible estimate is the one with the tighter interval.

title: Flexible estimation is presented as a remedy for identification failure
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Feuerriegel S, Frauen D, Melnychuk V, et al. Causal machine learning for predicting treatment outcomes. Nat Med 2024;30:958-968
States that causal machine learning supports individualized effect estimation only under the same identification assumptions as conventional methods, which is the claim applied work elides.


Target trial emulation under nonmutually exclusive assignment. Am J Epidemiol 2026;195(4):1045
Demonstrates empirically that poor overlap defeats advanced adjustment, which is the concrete form the general point takes.

title: Flexible estimation is presented as a remedy for identification failure
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Pair every flexible nuisance model with a support diagnostic reported for the conditioning sets the model actually uses, and state the support definition, since the diagnostic is only as meaningful as that definition. Score estimators on failure awareness: whether their diagnostics signal a severe positivity violation or a non-identifiable target, tested against deliberately non-identifiable simulation scenarios. Include at least one such scenario in every methods comparison, because an estimator that always returns a narrow interval is not robust if it never warns.

title: Flexible estimation is presented as a remedy for identification failure
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors agreed the problem is open and no counterevidence surfaced.
The source said. “Identification is a property of the observed data together with the assumptions, not a property of the estimator. A neural network cannot learn a counterfactual contrast that the data and assumptions do not identify, and flexible modeling that reduces approximation error in a nuisance function can at the same time disguise unsupported extrapolation, because a smooth fit extends confidently into regions with no observations. The distinction is stated clearly in the methodological literature and is repeatedly elided in applied work, where a more flexible learner is offered as the answer to a confounding or positivity concern. There is no diagnostic in common use that separates a flexible model interpolating where data exist from the same model extrapolating where they do not.”
What was wrong with it. Support and overlap diagnostics that flag particular forms of extrapolation do exist, so the claim that no diagnostic separates interpolation from extrapolation was too strong. They are definition-dependent and model-dependent, and they cannot certify sequential exchangeability, positivity or identification, which is the weaker and correct version.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): The corpus contains a growing body of flexible estimation inside emulations, including ensemble-learning marginal structural models and deep learning comparisons, and it contains no support diagnostic reported alongside a flexible nuisance model and no methods comparison that includes a deliberately non-identifiable scenario. A 2026 Nature Communications paper evaluates bias across statistical and deep learning methods in a heart failure emulation, which is the comparison the entry wants and does not include a non-identifiable arm. Failure awareness as a scored property does not appear anywhere.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. The corpus contains a growing body of flexible estimation inside emulations, including ensemble-learning marginal structural models and deep learning comparisons, and it contains no support diagnostic reported alongside a flexible nuisance model and no methods comparison that includes a deliberately non-identifiable scenario. A 2026 Nature Communications paper evaluates bias across statistical and deep learning methods in a heart failure emulation, which is the comparison the entry wants and does not include a non-identifiable arm. Failure awareness as a scored property does not appear anywhere. Cites 10.1038/s41467-026-74999-6: Compares flexible against conventional estimation for bias inside an emulation, which is the nearest existing test and does not include a non-identifiable scenario.. Cites 10.1002/bimj.70133: Applies ensemble learning to the weight model in a longitudinal setting, which is where the extrapolation concern applies..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The central identification claim is correct, although identification formally concerns the observed-data law, causal model, target estimand, and identifying assumptions rather than the realized finite dataset. Flexible estimation cannot repair failed exchangeability or positivity. The absolute diagnostic claim is too strong: propensity-score overlap, conditional treatment probabilities, density ratios, nearest-neighbor distances, leverage, and related support diagnostics can operationally flag extrapolation. They cannot certify identification, diagnose unmeasured confounding, or provide a model-free boundary between interpolation and extrapolation in high-dimensional longitudinal histories. Simulations can test warnings for deliberately detectable support failures, but no estimator can be required to detect every nonidentifiable target from the observed distribution alone. No package capability claim is present.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. Inverted search did not find a standard that closes this gap. Feuerriegel et al. (Nat Med 2024) restate that causal ML requires the same identification assumptions as classical methods and does not identify contrasts the data cannot support; that is prior art for the claim, not a solution. Hill and Su (Ann Appl Stat 2013) and Nethery et al. (Ann Appl Stat 2019) give BART-centered common-support diagnostics and nonoverlap-aware estimation, and propensity-score density/trim diagnostics remain routine for low-dimensional scores. Those tools do not constitute a diagnostic in common use that flags, for a general flexible nuisance (including neural nets) and for the same high-dimensional conditioning sets the nuisance uses, which predictions are interpolation versus extrapolation. Package activity in TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, lmtp, WeightIt, and related tools still emphasizes IPW weight extremity and classical overlap plots rather than per-prediction support maps for flexible outcome models. Failure-awareness scoring against deliberately non-identifiable simulations is not an established methods-comparison standard. The problem remains open as stated for applied flexible nuisance work; the caveat is that specialized support diagnostics for some nonparametric models already exist and should be named rather than implied to be nonexistent.

glm

open / supported. The claim correctly identifies that identification is a property of data and assumptions, not the estimator, and that flexible models can disguise extrapolation. The reason given for it being open (lack of common diagnostics for high-dimensional extrapolation) logically supports the claim. The claim is pitched at the right level of generality and correctly frames the issue as a current practice gap rather than a structural impossibility.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: Learned embeddings from clinical text can carry post-treatment information into a baseline adjustment set
text: LRN-03 Unverifiable High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: Learned embeddings from clinical text can carry post-treatment information into a baseline adjustment set
text:
Statement
Notes, imaging and device data capture severity, treatment rationale and outcomes that structured fields miss, and natural language processing has been proposed for eligibility extraction and phenotyping on that basis. A learned representation of a clinical note is a dense summary of everything in the note, which can include the site, the treating clinician’s behavior, protected characteristics and information about a treatment decision already made. An embedding whose input window is not demonstrably prior to both the assignment and the decision behind it can therefore carry post-treatment content into a nominal baseline adjustment set, and a timestamp preceding assignment does not establish that it does not. Formal treatment-leakage methods and text distillation exist and are not standard practice in emulations, and no routine test certifies that a representation encodes prognosis rather than the treatment that was about to be given.

title: Learned embeddings from clinical text can carry post-treatment information into a baseline adjustment set
text:
Why it is open
The causal role of an embedding dimension is not interpretable, so the standard remedy of inspecting an adjustment set does not apply. Predictiveness of treatment is the obvious test and settles nothing: a genuinely prognostic representation predicts treatment through confounding by indication, and a leaking one predicts it directly. Restricting to pre-assignment text bounds the leak without eliminating it, because a note written before treatment can describe a decision already taken, and validity therefore rests on auditable content provenance rather than on timing metadata.

title: Learned embeddings from clinical text can carry post-treatment information into a baseline adjustment set
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Wang, et al. An operational target trial emulation framework for causal inference using electronic health records. npj Digit Med 2026
Proposes natural language processing for eligibility extraction and phenotyping within an emulation framework.


Feuerriegel S, Frauen D, Melnychuk V, et al. Causal machine learning for predicting treatment outcomes. Nat Med 2024;30:958-968
Sets the boundary between predictive performance and causal validity that high-dimensional adjustment repeatedly crosses.

title: Learned embeddings from clinical text can carry post-treatment information into a baseline adjustment set
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use temporally locked encoders trained on content demonstrably prior to both the assignment and the treatment decision, and publish the provenance of that window in dates and document types rather than in prose. Adopt the existing treatment-leakage tests and text distillation methods rather than treating predictiveness as a diagnostic, and where a representation is used as a proxy, state the proximal role and the identification conditions it requires. Prefer interpretable proxy sets over indiscriminate adjustment for a high-dimensional representation whose causal role cannot be argued.

title: Learned embeddings from clinical text can carry post-treatment information into a baseline adjustment set
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source said. “Notes, imaging and device data capture severity, treatment rationale and outcomes that structured fields miss, and natural language processing has been proposed for eligibility extraction and phenotyping on that basis. The risk is specific: a learned representation of a clinical note is a dense summary of everything in the note, which can include post-treatment information, the identity of the site, the behavior of the treating clinician and protected characteristics. Adjusting for such a representation is adjusting for an object whose causal role is unknown and probably mixed, and the usual justification, that more information reduces confounding, does not hold when part of that information is a descendant of treatment.”
What was wrong with it. Two corrections. A timestamp preceding assignment is not sufficient: what matters is that the input window is demonstrably prior to both the assignment and the underlying treatment decision, which is a provenance requirement rather than a date check. And the entry’s proposed test, whether the embedding predicts treatment better than structured covariates do, neither establishes nor rules out leakage. Formal treatment-leakage methods and text distillation exist without being standard.
Dissent. grok dissented (overstated): The report frames embedding adjustment as an open risk without naming the literature that already defines and partially remediates it. Daoud, Jerzak, and Johansson (NAACL 2022) formalize treatment leakage when text is used as a confounder proxy, including leakage from pre-assignment documents that anticipate treatment. Daoud, Johansson, and Jerzak (arXiv:2601.02400, late 2025/2026) add formal definitions, four distillation methods (similarity passage removal, distant-supervision passage classification, salient-feature removal, iterative nullspace projection), and simulation plus empirical sensitivity analysis; they explicitly address the paradox that pre-timestamped text can still encode treatment. That is real prior art for detection and mitigation, not mere restatement. Residual openness remains for clinical TTE: methods are not standard in EHR phenotyping pipelines; Wang et al. (2026) still promote NLP for eligibility without a required leakage audit; temporal locking plus formal comparison of embedding-versus-structured treatment prediction is recommended in the agenda and only partially operationalized outside medicine. Sensitivity and distillation quantify or reduce leakage; they do not make an embedding’s causal role fully interpretable dimension-by-dimension. The problem is therefore partially solved in the text-as-confounder literature and still under-adopted in clinical emulation practice.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. A search for treatment leakage, temporal locking or auditing of learned representations used as adjustment sets returned nothing in the screened corpus. The claim is therefore unrefuted and weakly evidenced: the corpus is built from target trial and g-method phrases, and work on representation leakage would most likely appear in machine learning venues that none of the eight phrases reaches. The vote is open at the confidence ceiling this project sets for searched-and-found-nothing.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. An embedding derived from content observed after treatment assignment or after the clinical treatment decision can encode descendants of treatment and make baseline adjustment invalid. The risk is conditional on the source content and causal timing, not on representation learning or opacity by itself. A deterministic embedding of genuinely baseline variables remains baseline, and site or protected characteristics are not automatically invalid adjustment variables. Individual embedding dimensions need not be causally interpretable if the provenance and causal roles of their inputs are defensible. The proposed treatment-prediction test is not a valid leakage diagnostic: stronger prediction of assigned treatment can arise from additional legitimate confounder information, instruments, or actual leakage, and the test cannot distinguish these explanations. Likewise, merely declaring an embedding a proximal proxy is insufficient without valid proxy roles and the associated identifying conditions. No package capability claim is present.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / overstated. The report frames embedding adjustment as an open risk without naming the literature that already defines and partially remediates it. Daoud, Jerzak, and Johansson (NAACL 2022) formalize treatment leakage when text is used as a confounder proxy, including leakage from pre-assignment documents that anticipate treatment. Daoud, Johansson, and Jerzak (arXiv:2601.02400, late 2025/2026) add formal definitions, four distillation methods (similarity passage removal, distant-supervision passage classification, salient-feature removal, iterative nullspace projection), and simulation plus empirical sensitivity analysis; they explicitly address the paradox that pre-timestamped text can still encode treatment. That is real prior art for detection and mitigation, not mere restatement. Residual openness remains for clinical TTE: methods are not standard in EHR phenotyping pipelines; Wang et al. (2026) still promote NLP for eligibility without a required leakage audit; temporal locking plus formal comparison of embedding-versus-structured treatment prediction is recommended in the agenda and only partially operationalized outside medicine. Sensitivity and distillation quantify or reduce leakage; they do not make an embedding’s causal role fully interpretable dimension-by-dimension. The problem is therefore partially solved in the text-as-confounder literature and still under-adopted in clinical emulation practice. Cites https://aclanthology.org/2022.naacl-main.413/: Defines treatment leakage when text used for confounding adjustment also carries treatment signal, including leakage from pre-assignment future-referencing language; establishes the identification and estimation problem the agenda restates.. Cites arXiv:2601.02400: Provides formal statistical definitions of treatment leakage plus automatic and semi-automatic distillers and leakage sensitivity analysis so that text representations can be purged or stress-tested for treatment-predictive content before adjustment..

glm

open / overstated. The claim correctly identifies the risk of post-treatment leakage in learned embeddings. However, the assertion that ‘no test distinguishes’ a representation encoding prognosis from one encoding treatment is an overstatement of impossibility when it means that no standard or easily applicable test exists. It is a claim about current practice wearing the language of impossibility.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1/4) → R7:counter-and-support-both-present(support=1/counter=1)

title: Phenotypes enter emulations as error-free binary variables
text: MER-01 Unverifiable Very high priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Phenotypes enter emulations as error-free binary variables
text:
Statement
Prescriptions differ from dispensings and dispensings differ from ingestion; diagnostic codes differ from clinical events; death and care outside the system may be incompletely captured. When a treatment, a time-varying confounder, an eligibility criterion or an outcome is a latent clinical state and the emulation analyzes an error-prone thresholded proxy as though it were fixed, differential longitudinal misclassification distorts several things at once. An erroneous weight factor persists in the cumulative weights of every clone that remains at risk. Artificial-censoring membership changes as well, but only where the mismeasured variable enters the strategy, the eligibility rule or the censoring rule. Without validation information and assumptions that identify a joint measurement model and transport it to the analysis population, measurement bias and confounding bias cannot be uniquely separated. Emulation pipelines threshold at the start and propagate none of this.

title: Phenotypes enter emulations as error-free binary variables
text:
Why it is open
The interaction is nonlinear: misclassification of a time-varying confounder biases the weight and changes who is censored, so the bias does not decompose into a measurement part and a confounding part without further assumptions. Validation samples that would calibrate a phenotype are usually convenience samples from one site, and transporting a sensitivity and specificity across sites is itself an untested transport claim. Propagation is achievable without rebuilding the pipeline, by embedding a deterministic analysis in multiple imputation, posterior draws or a bootstrap, which makes the absence a matter of convention rather than of capability.

title: Phenotypes enter emulations as error-free binary variables
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Wang, et al. An operational target trial emulation framework for causal inference using electronic health records. npj Digit Med 2026
Describes validation-sample and probabilistic phenotype approaches to outcome misclassification in record-based studies.


Benz L, et al. Adjusting for selection bias due to missing eligibility criteria in emulated target trials. Am J Epidemiol 2025
Shows the shape of a validation-anchored correction for one protocol component, which is the template a phenotype correction would follow.

title: Phenotypes enter emulations as error-free binary variables
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Propagate phenotype uncertainty by embedding the existing deterministic pipeline in multiple imputation, posterior sampling or a bootstrap over the measurement model, which requires no new estimator and produces an interval that reflects the measurement. Develop validation-subsample targeted learning and Bayesian latent-class g-formula models for the cases where that is not enough, and state the transport assumption when a validation sample from one site calibrates another. Simulate sensitivity and specificity from 0.70 to 0.99 with differential misclassification odds ratios from 1 to 4, reporting bias in the estimated regime effect rather than in the phenotype, and establish how large a validation sample must be before the correction is worth its variance cost.

title: Phenotypes enter emulations as error-free binary variables
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source said. “Prescriptions differ from dispensings and dispensings differ from ingestion; diagnostic codes differ from clinical events; death and care received outside the system may be incompletely captured. Methods for outcome misclassification in electronic health records increasingly use validation samples and probabilistic phenotypes. Emulation pipelines almost universally do not: a phenotype is thresholded to a binary variable at the start and treated as truth thereafter. Differential misclassification then interacts with weighting and with time-varying confounding in ways that are not intuitive, because an error in the exposure at one time propagates into the weights at every later time, and no standard analysis propagates the phenotype uncertainty at all.”
What was wrong with it. The propagation mechanism was stated too loosely. An erroneous weight factor persists in the cumulative weights of clones that remain at risk, and artificial-censoring membership changes only when the mismeasured variable enters the strategy, the eligibility rule or the censoring rule; those are different channels. The entry also implied that a pipeline must accept probabilistic inputs natively, when a deterministic pipeline embedded in multiple imputation, posterior draws or a bootstrap achieves the same propagation.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): Searching for phenotype uncertainty propagated through an emulation returned discussions of misclassification as a listed threat and no pipeline that accepts probabilistic treatment or outcome nodes and carries the uncertainty to the final interval. Design-bias reviews name outcome misclassification among the biases to avoid without supplying the propagation. The entry’s specific claim, that the interaction between differential misclassification, weighting and time-varying confounding is not handled, is consistent with what the corpus shows. codex dissented (overstated): The underlying joint longitudinal measurement-error problem is real, but several assertions are too categorical. Prescribing, dispensing, and ingestion are distinct variables; their difference is misclassification only when the estimand targets one but the protocol measures another. In a cumulative inverse-probability weight, an erroneous treatment factor at time s remains in later cumulative products for a clone still at risk, but a clone artificially censored at s has no later weights. Mismeasurement of a time-varying confounder changes artificial-censoring membership only when that variable determines the dynamic strategy, eligibility, or censoring rule; under a static sustained strategy it can distort nuisance models without changing who is censored. The resulting biases can interact, but the defensible claim is that no unique identified additive measurement-versus-confounding decomposition generally exists without additional assumptions, not that no decomposition is possible. End-to-end propagation also does not require every estimator to accept soft inputs natively: multiple imputation, posterior draws, or a whole-pipeline bootstrap can wrap deterministic estimators. No package is named, so the claims about ‘almost universally,’ ‘no standard analysis,’ and ‘most implementations’ cannot be established from package ground truth. TrialEmulation 0.0.4.11 confirms one indicator-based implementation, not the asserted prevalence. The narrowed problem remains open, while uniformly assigning very-high severity is unjustified because importance depends on the estimand, error mechanism, validation information, and decision sensitivity.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. Searching for phenotype uncertainty propagated through an emulation returned discussions of misclassification as a listed threat and no pipeline that accepts probabilistic treatment or outcome nodes and carries the uncertainty to the final interval. Design-bias reviews name outcome misclassification among the biases to avoid without supplying the propagation. The entry’s specific claim, that the interaction between differential misclassification, weighting and time-varying confounding is not handled, is consistent with what the corpus shows. Cites 10.1136/bmjmed-2024-001280: Enumerates design-related biases including measurement, showing the problem is recognized within the framework without being handled quantitatively..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The underlying joint longitudinal measurement-error problem is real, but several assertions are too categorical. Prescribing, dispensing, and ingestion are distinct variables; their difference is misclassification only when the estimand targets one but the protocol measures another. In a cumulative inverse-probability weight, an erroneous treatment factor at time s remains in later cumulative products for a clone still at risk, but a clone artificially censored at s has no later weights. Mismeasurement of a time-varying confounder changes artificial-censoring membership only when that variable determines the dynamic strategy, eligibility, or censoring rule; under a static sustained strategy it can distort nuisance models without changing who is censored. The resulting biases can interact, but the defensible claim is that no unique identified additive measurement-versus-confounding decomposition generally exists without additional assumptions, not that no decomposition is possible. End-to-end propagation also does not require every estimator to accept soft inputs natively: multiple imputation, posterior draws, or a whole-pipeline bootstrap can wrap deterministic estimators. No package is named, so the claims about ‘almost universally,’ ‘no standard analysis,’ and ‘most implementations’ cannot be established from package ground truth. TrialEmulation 0.0.4.11 confirms one indicator-based implementation, not the asserted prevalence. The narrowed problem remains open, while uniformly assigning very-high severity is unjustified because importance depends on the estimand, error mechanism, validation information, and decision sensitivity.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. Inverted prior: searched for an end-to-end solution that lets sustained-strategy or time-varying TTE pipelines take probabilistic (non-thresholded) treatment, confounder, and outcome phenotypes and propagate differential misclassification through weights and censoring into the regime-effect interval. Nothing retrieved closes that full claim.


Own citations first. Wang et al. (npj Digit Med 2026; 10.1038/s41746-026-02563-z) is an operational TTE framework paper. Available text describes validation samples and probabilistic or uncertainty-aware outcome models as tools that can account for measurement error, and separately reviews g-methods for sustained strategies. It does not deliver a validated pipeline that accepts probabilistic treatment and outcome nodes end to end, nor simulations of regime-effect bias under differential time-varying misclassification. Description of existing pieces is not resolution. Benz et al. (Am J Epidemiol 2025; 10.1093/aje/kwae471; arXiv:2406.16830) targets selection bias from missing eligibility criteria via IPW under an MAR-type assumption for eligibility ascertainment. It is a useful template for validation-anchored IPW on one protocol component; it is not phenotype measurement-error correction for time-varying exposure or confounders.
Component prior art (does not close the stated gap). Hubbard, Tong, Duan, Chen (Epidemiology 2020; 10.1097/EDE.0000000000001193) give a hand-computable bias correction for continuous EHR probabilistic outcome phenotypes in association studies. Scope is outcome misclassification and association parameters, not time-varying treatment weights or sustained regimes. Edwards et al. (Am J Epidemiol 2018; 10.1093/aje/kwy028) fold sensitivity analysis for cause-of-death misclassification into the parametric g-formula; that is quantitative bias analysis, not identification with validation-anchored probabilistic nodes. Edwards et al. (RIME; PubMed 31971584, 2020) reparameterize imputation for exposure misclassification with validation data and illustrate combination with IPW for hazard ratios and risks: point-exposure misclassification with IPW, not full longitudinal differential error in exposure, confounders, and outcomes under dynamic or sustained strategies. Nab et al. (Epidemiology 2020) quantify bias from a misclassified confounder in MSM-IPW; characterization and QBA, not a solved TTE pipeline. Lu et al. (J Biomed Inform 2024; 10.1016/j.jbi.2024.104690) leverage multiple error-prone algorithm phenotypes plus a small validation set for risk-factor associations: again association, not TTE g-methods.
Material that strengthens openness. Ross, Cole, et al. (Epidemiology 2024; 35(2):196–207) document challenges of transporting measurement-error parameters (sensitivity, specificity, and related bias parameters) from external validation data: this supports the report’s claim that Se/Sp transport across sites is itself an untested or fragile transport claim, not a solved step.
Software (CRAN/GitHub scan). TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, gfoRmulaICE, lmtp, ltmle, survtmle, WeightIt, MatchIt, cobalt, ipw, adjustedCurves, riskRegression, and related Python stacks (zEpid, causallib, lifelines, scikit-survival) remain binary or continuous node pipelines for treatment and outcome after analyst thresholding. CRAN’s causal-inference task view points measurement-error tooling to sensitivity packages (e.g., episensr, EValue), not first-class probabilistic phenotype inputs inside sequential TTE or g-formula estimation. No merged PR or release note retrieved that closes end-to-end phenotype uncertainty in these packages through 2025–2026.
Queries run (representative): Wang operational TTE DOI and Nature page/PDF; Benz kwae471/arXiv; “probabilistic phenotype” + causal/IPTW/g-formula/lmtp/ltmle/TTE 2023–2026; measurement error misclassification + MSM-IPW / g-formula / time-varying / sustained strategy; Hubbard probabilistic phenotypes; Edwards RIME and g-formula misclassification; Ross transporting measurement error; CRAN/GitHub TrialEmulation gfoRmula lmtp measurement error; TARGET/ENCePP/FDA RWE measurement error guidance cross-check. Journals and preprint venues searched via web for 2024–2026 hits on those terms.
Caveat on support: the entry is faithful that standard TTE pipelines threshold phenotypes and that the nonlinear interaction of differential time-varying misclassification with weighting and censoring is not handled end to end. It would be overstated only if read as “no methods exist for any piece of phenotype error.” Pieces exist (outcome probabilistic correction in associations; exposure misclassification with IPW; g-formula outcome SA; transport problems formalized). None of those pieces, alone or as packaged software, solves the problem as stated for sustained-strategy emulation with uncertainty carried to the final interval.

glm

open / supported. The statement correctly identifies a methodological gap in target trial emulation using EHR data. It asserts that standard pipelines threshold phenotypes and do not propagate uncertainty, which is a claim about current practice rather than a structural impossibility. The reasoning given for it being open (nonlinear interaction of misclassification, transportability of validation samples, pipeline architecture limitations) is internally consistent and supports the claim being open. The scope is appropriate for a methodological research agenda, and the severity is proportionate to the risk of biased causal estimates.

Decision path

title: Censoring at death is applied as data cleaning rather than as an identifying assumption
text:
Statement
Death, treatment discontinuation and competing clinical events change what an outcome contrast means. ICH E9(R1) requires that intercurrent events be handled explicitly, and the causal competing-risks literature distinguishes total effects, controlled direct effects and separable effects, each answering a different question. Applied emulations default to cause-specific hazards or to censoring at the competing event. Censoring does not select among those estimands: it alters the observed-data analysis, and it corresponds to a hypothetical elimination of the competing event only when that intervention is well defined and its identification conditions hold, which is a claim the analysis has to make and defend. Estimators for competing events inside emulated trials exist and are being applied. Off-the-shelf support for joint recurrent-event and terminal-event contrasts under sustained strategies remains limited, and no reporting standard requires the censoring decision to be justified as an identifying assumption rather than executed inside data preparation.

title: Censoring at death is applied as data cleaning rather than as an identifying assumption
text:
Why it is open
The estimands differ in what they assume rather than in what they fit, so a wrong choice produces a well-behaved analysis of the wrong quantity and nothing downstream flags it. Separable effects require decomposing a treatment into components with separately meaningful effects, which is a substantive claim about the drug that most applied settings cannot support. The combination of recurrent and terminal events with sustained-strategy emulation is not worked out in available software, so an analyst who chooses correctly on competing risks may have no estimator for the regime they wanted.

title: Censoring at death is applied as data cleaning rather than as an identifying assumption

Work
What it contributes




ICH E9(R1) addendum on estimands and sensitivity analysis in clinical trials
Requires explicit specification of the strategy for each intercurrent event, which is the discipline that the emulation literature has not yet inherited.


lmtp: Non-Parametric Causal Effects of Feasible Interventions Based on Modified Treatment Policies. CRAN
Supports censored outcomes and competing risks for modified treatment policies, one of the few implementations where the competing event is part of the estimand rather than a preprocessing step.

title: Censoring at death is applied as data cleaning rather than as an identifying assumption
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Prespecify the estimand as a cumulative incidence, a restricted mean event-free time or a recurrent-event contrast, and name the intercurrent-event strategy for each competing event in the protocol. Require that any censoring at a competing event be justified as an identifying assumption, with the intervention it corresponds to stated and its conditions argued, which turns a data-cleaning line into a reviewable claim. Compare multistate g-computation, joint frailty models, separable effects and recurrent-event targeted learning on data generated with a known competing-event structure, and build the joint recurrent-and-terminal case for sustained strategies, which is the gap in available implementations.

title: Censoring at death is applied as data cleaning rather than as an identifying assumption
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
The source said. “Death, treatment discontinuation and competing clinical events change what an outcome contrast means. ICH E9(R1) requires that intercurrent events be handled explicitly, and the causal competing-risks literature distinguishes total effects, controlled direct effects and separable effects, each answering a different question. Applied emulations nonetheless default to cause-specific hazards or censor competing events without matching the estimator to the causal question, and recurrent and terminal events are seldom modeled jointly. The step where an analyst censors follow-up at death is an identifying decision that selects among these estimands, and it is normally executed silently inside data preparation, where no reviewer sees it as a decision at all.”
What was wrong with it. Censoring at a competing event does not select or identify an estimand. It changes the observed-data analysis, and it supports a hypothetical elimination estimand only when that intervention is well defined and its identification conditions hold. Calling the censoring step the choice of estimand was the wrong description of what it does.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): The methodological apparatus the entry asks for exists further than it allows. A 2026 Journal of Epidemiology paper treats causal inference from time-to-event data with dependent censoring, confounding and competing events together, and a 2025 Journal of Clinical Epidemiology paper works a trial emulation with competing risks in a surgical application. The entry’s claim is nonetheless about practice rather than method: that applied emulations default to cause-specific hazards or censor at competing events without matching the estimator to the question, and that censoring at death is executed inside data preparation. Nothing in the corpus contradicts that, and the reporting requirement the entry proposes does not exist. codex dissented (overstated): The central warning is valid and potentially high severity: handling death or another intercurrent event is part of defining the estimand, and total, controlled direct, and separable effects answer different questions. The entry is nevertheless conceptually imprecise. An estimand is defined by its counterfactual outcomes and contrast; identification assumptions are separate. Simply censoring at death does not select or identify one of those causal effects. Depending on the analysis, it can instead produce a cause-specific risk-set quantity or an unidentified hypothetical contrast. The claims that censoring is normally silent and that recurrent and terminal events are seldom modeled jointly are empirical frequency claims not established by the cited package source. Pinned lmtp source exports lmtp_tmle, lmtp_sdr, and lmtp_survival; accepts longitudinal treatment, censoring, and competing-risk nodes; incorporates competing-event status in its recursion; and tests two treatment times with two competing-risk times. Pinned gfoRmula source exports gformula_survival and static and implements sustained intervention risks with an explicit competing-event model and an option governing whether that event is treated as censoring. These implementations address competing risks under longitudinal strategies, but neither exposes an explicit joint recurrent-event and terminal-event estimand. The narrower implementation and protocol gap therefore remains. grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): Inverted-prior search shows the methodological core of OUT-01 is older and better equipped than a pure ‘open’ label implies, while the applied silence problem remains. Young, Stensrud, Tchetgen Tchetgen and Hernán (2020) already formalize that treating a competing event as censoring selects a controlled-direct-effect style question rather than a total-effect cumulative incidence, so the ‘identifying assumption vs data cleaning’ distinction is settled in the causal competing-risks literature. Software already embeds that choice for sustained or feasible longitudinal interventions: gfoRmula documents explicit options for competing events under time-varying treatment strategies, and lmtp implements time-to-event outcomes with competing risks for modified treatment policies, including a later ‘total effect’ option in version 1.5.0 (citing Díaz, Hoffman and Hejazi). Janvin, Young, Ryalen and Stensrud (2024) formalize causal estimands for recurrent events with and without a terminal competing event. None of that fully closes OUT-01 as stated. Applied primers still describe censor-at-death plus Fine-Gray sensitivity as common practice (Terman et al., 2025). ICH E9(R1) still governs trials more tightly than routine emulation protocols; TARGET (2025) improves TTE reporting generally but does not by itself force an intercurrent-event strategy for death the way E9(R1) does for trials. Separable effects remain a substantive product claim, not a software switch. Joint recurrent-plus-terminal estimation under longitudinal confounding is advancing (Prosepe et al., 2025 multistate g-computation; D’Alessio et al., 2026 arXiv g-computation for recurrent and semi-competing events with time-varying actions) but those are method papers and proposals, not field-wide defaults or head-to-head evaluations of multistate g-computation, joint frailty, separable effects and recurrent-event targeted learning on a known competing-event DGP. Net: estimator and formal estimand machinery for competing death under many sustained strategies exist; silent preprocessing and incomplete recurrent/terminal tooling keep the problem only partially solved. open / supported. The statement is internally consistent and proportionate.
